title: ATK — Axiomatic Theorem Kernel: A Unified Framework for Formal Mathematical Verification, Proof Certification, and Research Automation
abstract: ATK (Axiomatic Theorem Kernel) is a research framework designed to organize, formalize, audit, and manage mathematical proofs across multiple research domains. The system integrates theorem dependency analysis, symbolic mathematical representations, automated verification workflows, proof-assistant interoperability, and reproducible certification procedures. ATK distinguishes structural mathematical results, conditional demonstrations, unresolved mathematical obligations, and successfully kernel-verified theorems. The framework incorporates mechanisms for tracking source revisions, cryptographic hashes, verification states, mathematical dependencies, and formal certification records. Its research applications include formal investigations associated with the Riemann Hypothesis, P versus NP, Navier–Stokes equations, Yang–Mills theory, the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer Conjecture, the Hodge Conjecture, and related mathematical problems. ATK is presented as a research and proof-engineering framework. Its use does not, by itself, establish the resolution of any open mathematical conjecture.

title: Data and code for "Soft-sector localization and temporal readout in a mixed spherical landscape"
abstract: Reproduction package for the manuscript “Soft-sector localization and temporal readout in a mixed spherical landscape.” It is self-contained: the simulation model, the simulation outputs, the analysis code, the tables used in the paper, the validation records, and the figure builders are all included, and nothing outside the archive is needed to regenerate the reported numbers. Running `pip install -r requirements.txt` followed by `python run_analysis.py` verifies the simulation package against its own SHA-256 manifest, rebuilds every table, and asserts that all nine reference CSVs are reproduced numerically. `--numerical-smoke` additionally checks the tensor acceleration, the force and Hessian derivatives, and the recreation of one complete history from its seed. Two validation results are stated here because they bound the claims of the manuscript. (a) Step-size check at N=8 with 20 disorders and delta = 0.01, 0.005, 0.0025: writer-off soft-sector localization is stable (mean L0 = 0.703, 0.647, 0.676; every 95% lower bound above 2/7), whereas normalized retention D(1) = 0.010, -0.133, -0.263 and the matched-control contrast = -0.025, 0.044, -0.003 are not step-size stable and are reported as exploratory. No step-size check was run at N=16, 32, or 48. (b) Control replay at N=32 and N=48, 20 disorders per size, under a versioned numerical convention: all 40 anchors pass with zero state and readout error between two runs of that convention, and every archived history observable is reproduced to 1.1e-11. It is a determinism check and does not regenerate the archived control directions, which differ by up to 0.90 in individual cells. All 228 files are contained in the top-level folder "soft_sector_localization_data_and_code/"; run the commands from inside it.

title: 未提供标题
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training across autonomous vehicles (AVs) without sharing raw driving data, but excessive uplink/downlink communication over bandwidth-constrained vehicular-to-everything links and privacy leakage through gradient inversion attacks limit its deployment.This paper proposes Janus, a unified FL framework combining adaptive Top-K gradient compression with error feedback on the uplink, genuine additive homomorphic encryption (HE, not a noise-based proxy) for secure aggregation, and compressed global-model broadcasting on the downlink.On real KITTI object-detection labels with 20 non-IID clients, Janus matches FedAvg/FedProx/QSGD accuracy (95.34% ± 0.01% vs. 95.35%± 0.03%, 3 seeds) while cutting combined communication by 61.8%; the same saving (61.0%) is independently reproduced on CIFAR-10.A real Paillier HE implementation is verified exact (error below 10⁻⁶), and a genuine gradient-inversion attack (Deep Leakage from Gradients) shows raw gradients are reconstructed almost perfectly (relative error 0.0026) versus 0.0775 for Janus's compressed updates, with HE removing the attack surface entirely.The same communication saving is further reproduced on real KITTI camera images with a CNN roughly 24x larger than the tabular model and on a multimodal model fusing real camera and LiDAR features, alongside additional baselines (FedPAQ, DP-FedAvg), membership-inference and model-poisoning attacks, Markov-chain mobility, simulated network latency (61.9% reduction), an energy proxy (45.1% reduction), and a formal convergence analysis.To the authors' knowledge, this is the first vehicular-FL evaluation combining joint uplink-downlink compression with genuine HE-based privacy, validated through real cryptography, real privacy attacks, statistical testing, cross-dataset and cross-modality generalisation, and a convergence guarantee.

title: Dual-Stream Memory for Vision-Language-Action Policies
abstract: Memory-dependent manipulation requires a policy to track execution state and recover visual evidence that is no longer observable. We propose dual-stream memory for vision-language-action policies, assigning these requirements to complementary representations. A task-agnostic Gated DeltaNet compresses history into one temporal token, supervised by progress prediction and action-conditioned feature reconstruction. A task-conditioned retriever retains frames above a fixed relevance threshold; linear multi-scale fusion encodes each frame into sixteen spatial tokens. We then freeze the temporal compressor and jointly optimize retrieval and policy learning. Across sixteen RoboMME tasks, the complete model achieves 49.22% mean success versus 44.51% for the published FrameSamp+Modul reference, improving fourteen tasks and all four suite means. On four real-robot tasks, mean success reaches 62.5% versus 37.5%, with the largest gains on repeated actions requiring execution-stage discrimination. These results support combining execution context with selective visual access, while failures under cup swaps expose persistent identity tracking as an unresolved requirement.

title: Unified Generative Video Compression with Autoregressive and Bidirectional Video Diffusion
abstract: Video diffusion models can reconstruct visually compelling content from severely compressed representations at ultra-low bitrates, but they impose a rigid deployment trade-off. Bidirectional (BI) models achieve high quality through dense full-sequence attention, yet require the entire sequence before reconstruction and incur substantial latency. Autoregressive (AR) models enable low-delay streaming, but their restricted temporal context reduces compression efficiency. This tension is particularly relevant when a video stream must be decoded in real time yet is also stored for later, quality-oriented playback, making AR and BI models natural choices for the live and replay stages, respectively. To support both stages, we present UniGVC, a Unified Generative Video Codec that supports two decoding modes from a single bitstream. UniGVC-BI employs a BI-DiT with dense attention for quality-oriented random-access decoding, whereas UniGVC-AR uses windowed AR-DiT for low-delay streaming. Both paths share a hierarchical latent codec that recurrently produces the same conditions with ultra-low bitrates, allowing UniGVC-BI to serve as a conditional teacher for single-step distillation of UniGVC-AR. A tiny conditional video decoder further reduces streaming latency while preserving most of the reconstruction quality. On standard 1080p benchmarks, UniGVC-BI achieves the best overall rate-distortion-perception trade-off among the evaluated methods and produces temporally stable video at rates as low as 0.0005 bits per pixel. Meanwhile, UniGVC-AR remains competitive while decoding 1080p video at 36.85 FPS, over $250\times$ faster than UniGVC-BI. Code and models will be released later.

title: Pointwise Structures and Background Perturbation Analyses for Thermal Non-equilibrium Irrotational Flows in Three Space Dimensions
abstract: In this paper, both the pointwise space-time structures of the solution for a three-dimensional model describing gas dynamics in thermal non-equilibrium and the corresponding background stabilities within the L^p framework are investigated under the small initial perturbation assumption and the irrotationality condition. Our main tools are the modified Green's function according to the irrotationality condition, a priori energy method and a refined decay estimates of products composed of the entropy function and high-order derivatives.

title: RUBATO: Decoupled Clocks Allow Full-Duplex Models to Think as Fast as They Can
abstract: Recent Speech Full-Duplex (FDX) models are capable of engaging in naturalistic conversation by listening and speaking at the same time. Building on this foundation, recent architectures introduce internal thinking streams to enhance their intelligence. To guarantee these streams process successfully in real time, existing methods enforce a fixed decoding rate, which assumes a hardware profile capable of a specific latency. We argue this static approach is severely suboptimal. Because internal thinking is intrinsically asynchronous, an ideal FDX model should sustain real-time conversational flow while allowing each stream to decode at its own hardware-adaptive rate. Thinking streams must process as fast as the hardware allows to deliver accurate answers faster. To solve this, we propose RUBATO, a novel multistream positional encoding that assigns independent clocks to entirely decouple the streams. This structural isolation empowers the model to zero-shot interpolate across any inference decoding speed. It drastically simplifies dataset construction by requiring training on only two extreme decoding speeds while smoothly adapting to any intermediate rate during deployment. RUBATO demonstrates consistent robustness across five spoken reasoning tasks. On Spoken GSM8K, a baseline model collapses to 1.7% accuracy at interpolated speeds. Conversely, RUBATO-Full sustains 48.7% to 51.1% accuracy across all rates, leveraging faster hardware to achieve a 6.5x shorter time-to-answer with a constant time-to-first-response. This advantage holds on BIG-Bench Audio and amplifies significantly during complex full-duplex interruptions. Specifically, when a user interjects while the model is actively speaking and reasoning, RUBATO-Full achieves 40.0% to 45.1% accuracy, whereas the baseline fails completely.

title: When Generative Models Act as Simulators
abstract: A simulator summarizes an environment in a state that users can read and change. Generative models learn representations of the world without explicit specification, but offer no built-in way to edit that world's state. We investigate the conditions under which a generative model can act as a simulator through $\textit{editability}$: whether changing a model's latent representation produces the next-step outputs we get by editing a simulator's state. Plainly stated, our goal is to find a mapping between a generative model's latent state and the simulator state, where the model is trained on observations alone and the mapping is learned afterward. We test two kinds of mappings, both learned from observations paired with simulator states. In one, we train probes to decode the simulator state from the model, then steer along them. In the other, we learn the mapping directly with an inverse map, which can succeed even where steering fails. We study both in two contrasting environments: the discrete board game Othello, and Rayworld, our own continuous world of moving discs seen through partial renderings, closer to physical scenes and video. We find that which mapping succeeds depends strongly on the environment, even though the state is decodable in every variant. In Othello, editability falls smoothly as the game is simplified, and even small rule changes have large consequences. In Rayworld, probes fail to steer along the simulator's continuous state, yet an inverse map sets the model from that state anyway. A model can therefore be driven by a simulator it may have never learned.

title: AgentTune: A Unified Training Lifecycle for Tool-Using LLM Agents
abstract: Tool-using agents increasingly require a common substrate for building, training, evaluating, distilling, and maintaining agentic systems, yet existing tooling typically addresses these stages in isolation. We present AgentTune, a source-available Python library that provides a unified framework for developing and optimizing tool-using agents. At its core, AgentTune introduces a two-tier EventLog representation that preserves agent trajectories while supporting consistent projections for training, evaluation, and auditing. Building on this substrate, the library provides a shared agent runtime, tool-calling reinforcement learning, agentic distillation, retrieval-augmented generation, decision workflows, evaluation utilities, and a designed path toward self-healing agents. These components are exposed through composable interfaces so that agent strategies, training methods, evaluation procedures, and recovery mechanisms can be combined without requiring separate representations or pipelines. We demonstrate the framework across agentic tasks including legal contract search and domain-specific applications, illustrating its use for trajectory-based optimization, tool-use evaluation, and cross-task agent development. AgentTune is released as a source-available library at https://github.com/Lexsi-Labs/AgentTune

title: TreeHCA: Hindsight-Guided Exploration and Credit Assignment for Multi-Turn LLM Agents
abstract: Outcome-supervised group-relative policy optimization (GRPO) assigns the same advantage to every token in an LLM agent trajectory, leaving useful and unhelpful decisions undifferentiated. Hindsight credit assignment (HCA) can refine this feedback, but its estimates rely on trajectories containing informative alternatives at consequential histories. We introduce TreeHCA, which couples hindsight-guided exploration with hindsight credit assignment. TreeHCA uses changes in reference-answer likelihood to revisit intermediate histories and sample alternative continuations, forming a tree of reasoning and tool interactions. Because this exploration changes the distribution of sampled continuations, we derive the corresponding inverse-hindsight importance correction, including an exact finite-pool identity. We use this structure in a normalized tree backup that propagates terminal outcomes into turn-level advantages. This shared hindsight structure is TreeHCA's central design principle, linking informative exploration with hindsight-guided credit assignment. Across seven question-answering benchmarks and three Qwen backbones, TreeHCA outperforms all baselines in aggregate exact match, validating the effectiveness of paired exploration and credit assignment for multi-turn LLM agent training. Our code is available at github.com/TheBlackCat22/TreeHCA.

title: Correction Training for Diffusion Models
abstract: Iterative sampling in diffusion models can lead to error accumulation due to exposure bias. The denoiser is trained on real images interpolated with noise, but at inference its inputs are constructed from its own imperfect predictions from the earlier steps, something it has never seen at training time. This might be one reason diffusion models often struggle without additional help, such as CFG. We introduce a correction step for diffusion models which attempts to reduce this training-inference gap. The corrector takes the base model's prediction as input and is trained against the same ground-truth target. This makes correction an explicit learning task, with training inputs provided by the base model. During sampling, at each denoising step, we iteratively refine the denoiser's clean-sample prediction. This allows us to correct predictions at intermediate denoising steps, preventing early artifacts from persisting into the final sample. Although the corrector is trained only on predictions from the base denoiser, it can be applied repeatedly to its own outputs at inference for better results. This simple framework leads to substantial improvement in sample quality while largely preserving diversity. We evaluate our method across DiT, SiT, and JiT. Our method substantially improves upon previously reported FID scores for unguided generation and, notably, unconditional generation, where producing high-quality samples without guidance has been particularly challenging. Our method achieves performance competitive with classifier-free guidance (CFG), and combining correction with CFG further improves diversity and reduces oversaturation typical of CFG. Finally, we show that the additional inference cost of correction can be amortized by distilling the refined predictions back into the base diffusion model, retaining the quality gains without additional inference-time overhead.

title: ThinkDrag: Semantic Drag-Based Image Editing with Visual Reasoning
abstract: Drag-based image editing provides an intuitive interface for spatially controlled image manipulation by allowing users to specify handle and target points. Existing methods have made substantial progress through optimization-based, one-step, and feed-forward formulations, but they often interpret drag instructions as geometric displacements. This limits their effectiveness when the desired edit depends on interpreting image content and inferring a plausible semantic transformation from sparse point constraints. We introduce ThinkDrag, a unified multimodal framework for drag-based image editing with visual reasoning. ThinkDrag is trained to associate point constraints with meaningful object- and scene-level transformations, and can optionally produce an explicit reasoning trace that interprets the intended edit before image generation. This reasoning trace improves interpretability, particularly for ambiguous drags. Drag Endpoint Markers, motivated by an analysis of cross-image attention, provide an explicit correspondence signal that grounds each drag in image space. To support this framework, we construct a supervised dataset of semantic drag transformations paired with reasoning traces and introduce DragBench++, a benchmark targeting challenging drag-based editing scenarios with reference edit solutions. Experiments show that ThinkDrag achieves state-of-the-art performance, improving generation quality and plausibility while maintaining competitive point-following precision.

title: GIST: Generator-state-Informed Supervision for Tabular Foundation Models
abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) based on prior-data fitted networks typically use sampled hard query labels, leaving avoidable sampling variability in pretraining. A key observation is that intermediate generator states can reveal label uncertainty beyond a sampled outcome. We propose Generator-state-Informed Supervision for TFMs (GIST), which uses these states to average query losses over conditional label distributions. GIST jointly designs task generation and query supervision, using entropy-calibrated encodings to obtain tractable, input-consistent targets on supported label-dependent branches. We show that this averaging preserves the population objective and yields no larger gradient covariance at fixed parameters within each generating distribution. Under matched pretraining schedules, GIST improves mean rank across three architectures on both TabArena and TALENT without changing architecture or inference. Across these benchmarks and architectures, GIST wins 62.1% of paired dataset-level comparisons against the corresponding hard-label controls.

title: Rethinking Leadership Decision Quality in AI-Augmented Strategic Business Environments: Toward an Integrated Multidisciplinary Framework
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in strategic business decision-making through predictive analytics, pattern recognition, forecasting, generative AI, and decision support systems. These capabilities expand organisational analytical capacity, but analytical capacity does not by itself constitute strategic decision quality; strategic decisions also require contextual interpretation, leadership judgment, appropriate reliance on AI, accountability, and adaptation under uncertainty. title: Formal Encoding of Nondeterministic Turing Machines and Structural Complexity Certificates in Lean 4
abstract: This research develops a formal framework for representing nondeterministic Turing-machine computations and associated complexity-theoretic constructions in Lean 4. The investigation includes tableau encodings, transition constraints, weight estimates, structural witnesses, and formal dependency chains relevant to computational complexity. Particular attention is given to the verification of auxiliary lemmas, the identification of conditional assumptions, and the distinction between formal equivalences and unconditional complexity lower bounds. The work contributes to the formal organization and verification of complexity-theoretic arguments without claiming a resolution of the P versus NP problem.

title: Robust Face Recognition and Morphing Defense Through Hyperspherical Manifold Hardening
abstract: Abstract Modern face recognition systems are widely deployed in high-security environments, such as automated border control and mobile authentication. However, these systems remain vulnerable to two primary security threats: adaptive adversarial perturbations, where minor pixel modifications cause misidentification, and structural face morphing, where blended composite images deceive biometric scanners. In this paper, we address the limitations of traditional lightweight models that suffer from spatial manifold crowding and decision boundary collapse under multi-step attack pressures. We propose a unified defense framework that integrates Adversarial Geodesic Loss with Smooth Softplus Margin regularization on a high-capacity pre-trained IResNet-100 backbone. By forcing the network to dynamically defend against online Projected Gradient Descent trajectories during training, our approach reshapes the latent hypersphere without sacrificing feature separability. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that our hardened pipeline achieves an absolute zero-percent bypass rate against landmark-aligned Delaunay triangulation morphing and restricts white-box adaptive attack success, while maintaining a pristine one-hundred-percent verification true acceptance rate for genuine users. This study establishes a robust, scalable defense mechanism that satisfies strict transaction standards for high-security biometric deployments. Keywords—Biometric security, face recognition, face morphing attacks, adversarial robustness, hyperspherical embeddings, geodesic distance, deep learning defense.

title: Artifact for "Mosaic: From Language Fragments to Program Logics"
abstract: Artifact for the POPL 2027 paper "Mosaic: From Language Fragments to Program Logics" by Max Vistrup, Klaus Kraßnitzer, Michael Sammler and Ralf Jung.Mosaic is a framework for building programming languages from reusable fragments: each fragment covers one feature of a language with its syntax, semantics and program logic rules, and a composed language automatically inherits the program logic rules of its fragments. - README.md: instructions for the artifact evaluation (start here)- mosaic.tgz: the sources, with a build script and the Dockerfile of the image- mosaic_image.tar.gz: a Docker image for x86-64 and ARM with the development pre-built, and VS Code with VsRocq in the browser- generation_data.txt: pinned commit hashes of the included repositories- SHA256SUMS: checksums of the files above The development is also available at https://gitlab.mpi-sws.org/iris/itree-program-logic/tree/mosaic.

title: An Agent Framework for Land Resource Monitoring and Analysis
abstract: This paper proposes an agent framework for land resource monitoring and analysis. The framework organizes and encapsulates domain knowledge and operational workflows into standardized skill units, enabling the agent to perform task planning, execution, and reflection under skill-based constraints and thereby improving the procedural consistency of complex operational tasks. In addition, a task-semantics-based result verification module is introduced to assess the semantic consistency of intermediate results and further identify latent errors in which tools execute successfully but the resulting outputs deviate from user requirements. Experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms the ReAct, Plan-and-Execute, and Plan-and-React baselines overall, achieving a final result accuracy of 93.33% ± 1.44%. Ablation experiments demonstrate that skill-based constraints, progressive loading, and result verification all improve agent execution reliability. A dedicated evaluation of the result verification module further shows that it can effectively identify latent execution errors, achieving a Precision of 93.55%, a Recall of 90.63%, and a false-positive rate of 6.25%.

title: Before They Ask: Anticipating Help-Seeking from Behavioral Signals in Virtual Reality
abstract: Immersive virtual reality (VR) is increasingly used for training and has the ability to track learner behavior continuously. Yet support is usually delivered only once a learner asks for it, and help is not always sought when needed. While support based on performance is common, less is known about detecting an emerging need for help from non-verbal behavior. We examined whether an upcoming help request can be anticipated from movement and gaze alone. We analyzed data from 21 participants who completed a VR assembly task in which rules changed without warning and could be consulted through a deliberate, logged action. All models were evaluated on unseen participants. Trial-level prediction was accurate but relied mainly on task outcomes, such as errors and earlier consultations, rather than on the learner’s ongoing behavior. Using short, continuously updated windows of movement and gaze, the model reached an AUC-PR of 0.159 against a chance level of 0.064, about 2.5 times the chance level, and most of its discriminative ability remained when the final turn toward the source of help was excluded. Before a request, movement slowed, gaze stayed closer to the head’s forward direction, and fixations lengthened. Help-seeking is thus partly foreshadowed by behavior VR systems already record, though the signal is still weak when generalized to new learners, who varied substantially in how often they sought help.

title: Neurons++: A Unified Visual-Stream Framework for Image and Video Reconstruction from fMRI with Neural-to-Visual Interpretability
abstract: Decoding visual experience from fMRI is important for understanding human perception and developing brain-computer interfaces. Recent generative decoding methods can reconstruct plausible images and videos, but visual plausibility alone does not ensure that the output is faithfully grounded in brain activity. In this work, we propose Neurons++, a visual-stream fMRI reconstruction framework for both static image and dynamic video reconstruction. Compared with our conference version Neurons, Neurons++ extends the paradigm from video-only reconstruction to visual-stream reconstruction for both images and videos, and replaces parallel task conditioning with serial cortex-inspired decoding. The model first uses image-fMRI pretraining to obtain a stable spatial-semantic initialization, and then performs subject-specific fine-tuning for image and video reconstruction separately. The serial design organizes fMRI-derived representations into explicit spatial, semantic, language-level, and temporal cues. Extensive experiments show that Neurons++ achieves state-of-the-art video reconstruction and competitive image reconstruction across standard benchmarks. Beyond reconstruction fidelity, neural-to-visual analyses indicate that Neurons++ exhibits qualitative directional controllability under neural perturbation, that its fMRI encoder read-out is sensitive to stimulus-relevant cortical features, and that it supports ROI-guided semantic modulation. Code and model weights are available at: https://github.com/xmed-lab/NeuronsPlusPlus.

title: Don't Guess, Just Ask: Evaluating Interactive Requirement Clarification for Repository-Level Software Development
abstract: As LLMs become increasingly capable of implementing software, a critical bottleneck emerges: whether they truly understand what users want. Users often begin with vague intent, leaving important requirements to be clarified through interaction. In repository-level development, misunderstandings can propagate and cause costly rework. However, existing benchmarks typically evaluate implementation from complete specifications or underspecified requests, overlooking pre-coding requirement clarification. Prior clarification studies mainly focus on function-level tasks. It therefore remains unclear how well LLMs can transform vague intent into clear requirements through interaction and how this capability affects subsequent code generation. We introduce ReqClarifyBench, an interactive requirement clarification benchmark for repository-level software development. It contains 341 tasks spanning game, miniapp, and web development, each with a vague user intent, a human-validated requirement document, and code evaluation artifacts. We employ LLM-based user simulators with diverse personas derived from real-world conversations. We evaluate six LLMs in terms of clarification effectiveness and generated requirement document quality. Results show that stronger clarification effectiveness does not necessarily translate into higher document quality, and performance varies substantially across user personas. We also find that coding-agent harnesses do not further improve requirement document quality compared with their base LLMs. These findings offer insights for building LLM-based end-to-end software development systems.

title: Scalable Learning of Determinantal Point Processes with Kernel-Structured Interactions
abstract: Determinantal point processes (DPPs) on a finite set are probability models that exhibit repulsion where inter-item similarities are encoded by a positive definite kernel matrix. Scaling DPP learning to large datasets typically requires imposing structural constraints on the kernel matrix, such as a low-rank-plus-diagonal form. However, structural assumptions introduce a severe trade-off between expressive power and computational scalability. Our study addresses this challenge by (a) modeling the full-rank interactions via a nonlinear kernel function and latent features, (b) designing a surrogate function for the maximum likelihood estimator, and (c) adopting stochastic optimization using random features of the nonlinear kernel. Numerical experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that our method significantly improves this trade-off, achieving better generalization performance with remarkable parameter efficiency.

title: KV-Repurpose: A Testbed for Evaluating Non-Prefix KV-Cache Reuse
abstract: KV-cache reuse in large language model serving is commonly limited to exact prompt prefixes, preventing reuse when the same retrieved document appears after different system prompts, conversation histories, or dynamic metadata. We present KV-Repurpose, an open-source, vLLM-based system for developing and evaluating segment-wise KV-cache reuse beyond exact prefixes. The system combines cache-aware segment scheduling, prompt construction, capacity management, workload generation, and runtime monitoring. Experiments on long-context benchmarks show that naive segment reuse largely preserves output quality for single-document question answering and summarization, while exposing clear limitations in cross-document reasoning. Under a Zipfian RAG-style workload in which 20% of requests share a fixed prefix, KV-Repurpose achieves a substantially higher token-level cache hit rate than prefix caching at the same 30 GB cache capacity, 63.9% versus 3.3%, resulting in lower TTFT. Even with 1 TB of cache capacity, prefix caching reaches only a 17.9% hit rate in this workload. Source code is available under the Apache-2.0 license at https://github.com/taiga333/eval-kv-repurpose.

title: Structure-Aware Numerical Stabilization for Half-Precision Proximal Policy Optimization
abstract: Local online training on resource-constrained platforms requires low computational and training-state overhead. We study the numerical stability and computational efficiency of half-precision proximal policy optimization (PPO) on commodity GPUs. Directly converting PPO training to FP16 is unreliable because numerical errors feed back through policy updates and subsequent data collection, while PPO repeatedly compares a current policy with a fixed behavior policy. We propose PPO-FP16 with three structure-aware modules. Global scalar protection stabilizes statistics shared across a minibatch or parameter update. Policy-change residual protection extracts and preserves small differences between the current and behavior policies. Efficient persistent-update protection stabilizes optimizer state and parameter writeback while reducing state storage. These changes preserve the PPO objective, hyperparameters, and training budget. Across six continuous-control tasks and five seeds, PPO-FP16 achieves the lowest mean return-AUC rank (1.90) among the four methods and ranks first in 17 of 30 environment-seed comparisons. Eight of nine performance configurations yield PPO update speedups ranging from 1.16 to 2.03 times. Relative to Full FP32 Adam, optimizer-state memory is reduced by 71.7 to 74.9 percent, and peak allocated GPU memory is reduced by up to 44.5 percent. The results show that protecting a small set of structurally important quantities can deliver stable, efficient FP16 PPO without retuning.

title: Manifold Navigation Learning Using Recurrent Networks: Efficient Training Techniques
abstract: Position tracking is a well-studied problem in Euclidean navigation, yet comparatively little attention has been given to navigation on general manifolds, where motion is governed by the underlying geometry of the space. In this work, we formalize the problem of manifold navigation as a velocity-driven tracking task and propose a coordinate-chart-based learning framework in which learning models operate entirely in a Euclidean representation. Predicted trajectories are mapped to the manifold via an immersion function prior to error computation, allowing geometric consistency to be evaluated without explicitly enforcing manifold constraints during learning. Within this framework, we focus on Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) for sequential position prediction on curved manifolds after comparisons with alternative recurrent architectures. We evaluate our GRU models, trained with pertinent custom loss functions, against both a standard MSE loss function and a naive vector-addition baseline. We evaluate our approach on both analytically (and numerically) defined manifolds, as well as a surface reconstructed from a LiDAR point cloud. Our results show that recurrent models can learn to approximate manifold-constrained dynamics from velocity sequences and consistently outperform Euclidean baselines. Our results demonstrate that certain custom loss functions significantly improve long-horizon prediction accuracy compared to conventional point-wise loss functions.

title: multi-llm-sphere-orchestration-provisional-benchmark
abstract: This sphere is a reproducible benchmark artefact created during repository orchestration. It is not proof of invariant geometry, AGI, harmonic truth or the final organism architecture. The author defines multi-LLM harmonised focus as hypothetical cancellation of drift, not an observed output. Independent cross-model convergence, harmonic invariant discovery and AGI were not measured. Symbolic LLMAdapter fixtures are not external model inference; historical exact model identities are unknown. The currently identified orchestrator is recorded only for checkpoint preparation. The archive preserves unchanged previously public numerical and native sphere packages, available prompt transcriptions and timestamps, a disclosure-limited public provenance ledger, commit and branch references, constructor/orchestration bias analysis, six-limb contracts, an Invariant Surface moving-manifold specification and a guarded Copilot handoff. The complete available private source inventory, source pins and lineage remain in the private checkpoint; raw tool logs, protected upstream sources, private keys, encrypted snapshots and architecture artwork are excluded. The checkpoint tag is multi-llm-sphere-orchestration-provisional-benchmark at commit 38e8525e03b0955a6ea281dd98921a1b0c11bcc8. Active GitHub ruleset 24814369 blocks updates and deletion with no bypass actors. Administrators can change that rule; protection is not cryptographic signing, blockchain anchoring or write-once retention. The later private draft motion branch moves 28 generated alignment files without changing their bytes and tests a bounded translating-plane reference; those branch changes are not merged, not a complete harmonic organism and not included as new runtime code in this checkpoint archive. Only the sphere-orchestration episode is designated a documented provisional state. The research programme, moving topology, curved-manifold transport, harmonic operator and high-energy-site validation remain open. Geometric reproduction does not prove invariant truth, intelligence, AGI or physical accuracy. The public architecture and website remain in their prior record; this publication does not deploy the live website.

title: ORYNTHRA-H6: Branch-Covariant Compression and an Exact Representation-Deficit Law for Bosonic Memory
abstract: ORYNTHRA-H6 develops a mathematical framework connecting task-relative compression, future executable transformations, representation theory, and the conserved spectral structure of bosonic memory. Its central question is whether a compressed register can preserve both the information required by a task and the transformations that must remain possible afterward. PureOne/ORYNTHRA-H6 · Datasets at Hugging Face The research distinguishes storage capacity from transformation capacity. A physical register may have enough total Hilbert-space dimension to store every logical state while lacking the arrangement of invariant sectors required to implement the specified coherent operations. ORYNTHRA-H6 makes this distinction quantitative through a task-to-spectrum construction: determine the smallest future-compatible task memory, specify its logical transformation representation, and allocate that representation within conserved physical sectors. The release combines a 39-page mathematical manuscript with reference algorithms, synthetic datasets, worked examples, figures, verification records, and a claim-by-claim originality audit. Future-compatible compression. Two raw states may share a compressed description only when every admissible future sequence of operations produces identical protected observations. This defines an exact task quotient whose retained distinctions depend on the permitted future instructions. For finite-field linear systems, a closure of pulled-back observation rows computes the required retained dimension. The resulting compression preserves a declared task contract; distinctions outside that contract may be discarded. Conserved-sector representation packing. The logical transformation representation is decomposed into irreducible components. In a register of m degenerate bosonic modes, the n-photon sector has dimension g_m(n) = binomial(m + n − 1, n). Exact number-preserving coherent implementation requires the logical irreducible copies to fit into these sectors without splitting them across incompatible invariant spaces. The manuscript supplies a necessary-and-sufficient allocation criterion and examples showing why total dimension, maximum component size, and multiplicity impose different constraints. Exact representation-deficit law. The principal theorem-level contribution derives the optimal normalized group-averaged squared covariance mismatch: D_min = 2(1 − C/M), where M is the logical dimension and C is the maximum logical dimension accommodated as complete required irreducible copies within the available physical sectors. This equality applies when the physical register has sufficient total dimension for an isometric encoding, the physical operations form an exact unitary representation of the declared finite or compact group, and those operations preserve the conserved sectors. Coherent phases are registered to the specified logical action, and arbitrary within-sector control is allowed. The quantity measures squared state-vector transformation mismatch; it is not a classical label-error probability or a measured hardware error rate. The law turns an allocation obstruction into an exact optimum. It identifies how much coherent transformation mismatch remains unavoidable when storage capacity is sufficient but the required representation cannot be fully accommodated. Explicit storage-versus-control frontiers. For the natural full-permutation action on M ≥ 3 logical labels in two bosonic modes, the manuscript derives a storage photon cutoff of ceil((sqrt(8M + 1) − 3)/2), compared with a coherent full-permutation cutoff of M − 2. Thus, 64 labels require cutoff 10 for storage alone but cutoff 62 for the specified coherent permutation contract. For 4,096 labels, the corresponding cutoffs are 90 and 4,094. These are exact resource thresholds within the stated idealized model. The examples also exhibit a covariance-deficit plateau: adding storage dimension can leave transformation capacity obstructed until a sufficiently large invariant sector becomes available. The H6 simplex register. Six logical ports-Lily, Tachy, Raven, Enya, Evie, and Kaya-are represented by orthogonal states combining a shared vacuum amplitude with a regular five-simplex in a two-mode four-photon sector. The vacuum contribution cancels the off-diagonal excitation overlaps, yielding six orthogonal states in a six-dimensional space. Each label has mean photon number 10/3. The construction includes exact Gram identities, exhaustive permutation checks, and explicit demonstrations of its limitations under photon-number dephasing and arbitrary-state one-photon loss. Instruction activation and compression instability. A separate six-generator construction acts on 36 binary coordinates. Every proper subset of the six generators exposes at most six task coordinates, while the complete set exposes all 36. Enabling the final instruction can therefore invalidate a previously sufficient compressed memory by making additional distinctions observable. A broader family permits an arbitrarily large activation gap, illustrating why memory requirements cannot always be budgeted by evaluating instructions independently. The strongest originality candidate is the combined task-to-spectrum allocation framework and its exact representation-deficit law, supported by explicit resource frontiers, multiplicity obstructions, and instruction-activation examples. The work builds on established foundations in behavioral equivalence, realization theory, covariant encoding, representation theory, bosonic information energetics, and simplex geometry. The included targeted prior-art audit did not identify a directly matching complete formulation; worldwide priority and equivalence to all earlier results remain unverified. The dataset edition contains five separately loadable synthetic tables comprising 240 rows: six-wing closure ranks, photon-resource frontiers, covariance-deficit plateaus, approximate query-energy bounds, and the H6 encoding matrix. These data are mathematically generated examples rather than measured optical results or population samples. title: From Individual Chatbot Interaction to the Virtual Tutor with Physical Presence: Comparing Educational Interaction Models with Conversational AI
abstract: Conversational artificial intelligence can provide individual study support, but the educational significance of its responses depends on how they are examined and used. We develop a conceptual framework comparing Individual Chatbot Interaction and Standard Classroom Interaction, then specify a Virtual Tutor with Physical Presence as a situated implementation of shared AI inquiry. The framework draws on selected scholarship concerning mediated learning, educational dialogue, self-regulation, cognitive engagement, pedagogical agents, and AI literacy. We define the unit of analysis as an interaction episode and distinguish private consultation, shared instruction, and hybrid activities through observable criteria. The tutor is specified as an animated avatar projected by video-mapping onto a static volumetric surface in the classroom; perceived presence and learning are treated as outcomes requiring measurement. The proposed contribution is a design specification linking public AI responses, teacher orchestration, evidence-based scrutiny, and individual reflection. An explanatory pathway connects these conditions to possible cognitive and metacognitive processes, with four propositions and matched comparisons for future evaluation. A projected avatar is neither necessary nor sufficient for collective verification, and its incremental value must be tested against simpler shared interfaces. No empirical effectiveness is claimed. The framework provides a basis for investigating when a situated conversational tutor supports disciplinary understanding and critical AI use.

title: Advanced hybrid metaheuristic framework for spiral rubber tapping trajectory optimization on curved tree trunks
abstract: Automated rubber tapping requires accurate reconstruction of smooth and kinematically feasible trajectories from discrete tapping points on complex curved trunk surfaces. However, achieving a balance between geometric smoothness and fitting accuracy remains challenging. This study proposes an optimization-driven trajectory modeling framework that integrates an Adaptive RIME algorithm with Bézier curve parameterization (ARIME-Bézier). While Bézier curves inherently ensure geometric continuity, their performance strongly depends on polynomial degree and control point configuration. To overcome this limitation, the proposed Adaptive RIME incorporates an adaptive hard-rime puncturing mechanism and a time-varying step-size strategy to mitigate premature convergence. The framework jointly optimizes the polynomial degree and control point distribution, enabling a balanced trade-off between statistical fitting precision and kinematic smoothness required for stable robotic tapping. Experimental validation is conducted on a standard spiral tapping path (32° slope angle, 80 mm trunk radius, 180° wrap angle). Comparative results demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms baseline approaches, achieving R² > 0.90 across all cases. The model attains a root mean square error of 5.9137, with average radial and slope angle deviations of 0.8% and 1.74%, respectively. These findings confirm the robustness and practical applicability of the proposed framework for intelligent robotic rubber tapping systems.

title: A scalable sample-based quantum diagonalization solver for general Pauli-sum Hamiltonians
abstract: A scalable ground-state solver to be used in sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) is presented. The solver is built on JAX API, and is intended to be run on GPU platforms and possibly many-GPU high-performance computing facilities. It is capable of subspace diagonalization in up to $2^{30}$-dimensional subspace, with possible upgrades to enable even larger-scale operations. The two main components, a general-purpose eigensolver and an SQD-specific matrix-vector operation function, are described in detail. Efficiency of the eigensolver with respect to the GPU memory is demonstrated using a simple physics model. Furthermore, good strong scaling of the eigensolver in many-GPU environment is observed.

title: Gaussian Splatting with Reflections Guided by What is Seen
abstract: While novel view synthesis methods like Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) have shown impressive performance on common scenes, they often struggle with capturing view-dependent specular effects, particularly near-field reflections. Existing methods utilize environment maps, which only represent lights from infinity, or environment Gaussians, which rely solely on indirect supervision from reflections, are insufficient for accurately modeling such effects. Here, we propose a framework based on 2D Gaussian Splatting (2DGS) that leverages directly observable environment information in input images. Our approach also integrates a hybrid reflection appearance representation and view-dependent specular modeling. Experiments on public benchmarks and a newly curated near-field reflection dataset demonstrate that our method achieves superior rendering quality and geometric accuracy.

title: Frontend-Assisted Large Audio-Language Models for SLT2026 SmartGlasses Challenge
abstract: This paper describes our systems for the Track 1 time-stamped speaker-attributed ASR task of the SmartGlasses Challenge. To handle overlapping speech, background noise and far-field conditions in two-person conversations, we employ SoulX-Transcriber, a multimodal large language model that takes full-length audio as input and generates structured transcriptions. In addition, we investigate the effect of speech frontend processing, including a rule-based Guided Source Separation method and a data-driven speech separation model, both of which improve performance on the validation set. Considering inference stability, our final submission uses the fine-tuned SoulX-Transcriber system, achieving a tcpCER of 6.22 on the test set.

title: Beyond a Single Crop: Contextualized Embeddings for Player Re-Identification
abstract: Person re-identification is typically addressed by learning identity-discriminative embeddings from individual person crops. However, player re-identification in broadcast sports videos presents a unique challenge: players from the same team often share similar appearances, while video sequences provide repeated observations of the same players under different viewpoints and surrounding contexts. Existing crop-based approaches largely ignore this contextual information, which can be critical for resolving visually similar identities. Here, we propose ContextReID, a contextualized embedding framework that represents a player by jointly considering other players in the same frame and observations from different frames of the broadcast sequence. By incorporating both co-occurring players and cross-frame observations, the model learns identity features relative to the surrounding visual context rather than relying only on isolated appearance cues. We implement this framework with a vision-language model that takes sets of player crops as input and generates context-aware embeddings for individual players. A combined contextual learning and retrieval objective encourages the model to capture cross-frame identity relationships while maintaining discriminative embeddings for player matching. Experiments across three multi-object tracking benchmarks show that ContextReID improves player retrieval over conventional single-crop embedding approaches in both Rank-1 and mAP. These results highlight the utility of spatial and temporal context for reliable player identification in broadcast sports videos.

title: MagCilia: A Compact Magnetociliary Tactile Sensor with 3D Force Sensing for Robotic Contact Perception and Grasping Feedback
abstract: Robotic grasping and surface exploration benefit from simultaneous measurement of normal and tangential forces and from surface information obtained through contact. Here, we present a compact magnetociliary tactile sensor (MagCilia) that combines a flexible magnetic-cilia structure with a Hall sensor for 3D force sensing. Quasi-static finite element analysis is used to investigate structural deformation and magnetic responses under multidirectional loading. To reconstruct forces from the coupled magnetic channels, we propose causal history fusion regression (CHFR), which combines current magnetic-field measurements with their recent changes. Five-fold cross-validation grouped by calibration record yields root-mean-square errors of 0.40, 0.57, and 0.69 N for Fx, Fy, and Fz, respectively, with corresponding coefficients of determination of 0.93, 0.90, and 0.92. Robotic experiments demonstrate tangential-force-guided gripper adjustment and multi-axis load monitoring under external perturbations. Frequency-domain features of the reconstructed forces distinguish six surface categories with 99.39% accuracy in three-fold cross-validation grouped by acquisition session. An online robotic demonstration additionally identifies all six tested surfaces. These results demonstrate 3D force reconstruction, grasping feedback, and surface recognition using a single compact tactile unit.

title: zip2zip++: Towards Inference-Time Token Compression with Minimal Quality Loss
abstract: Dynamic vocabularies built on-the-fly via Lempel-Ziv-Welch (LZW) compression let a language model represent the same text in fewer tokens, but prior work shows that this efficiency comes at a cost to reasoning and perplexity. We show that this quality gap is not a fundamental price of compression but can be substantially closed through targeted improvements to the compression layer and LZW codec, without modifying the underlying pretrained language model. Our analysis reveals four key issues: (1) LZW's compression algorithm creates an implicit conflict between the input embedding and the output embedding, a tension that a single shared embedding cannot resolve; (2) naively applying RoPE to LZW-compressed sequences ignores that merged tokens can span multiple tokens; (3) merging certain tokens (notably digits) disproportionately hurts downstream accuracy; and (4) dynamic vocabularies introduce an inherent segmentation ambiguity that confounds standard evaluation. We address these through decoupled input/output dynamic embedding layer, size-aware RoPE positioning, and a modified LZW codec supporting selective merges and multi-view segmentations. Across four models, our recipe improves perplexity on every corpus we evaluated as well as mathematical reasoning accuracy, closing roughly half the quality gap between zip2zip and the uncompressed baseline at a similar compression ratio on general text. This represents a significant step toward lossless adaptive-vocabulary compression for language models.

title: MORAD: Reinforcement Learning with Multi-Objective Rewards for RNA Inverse Design
abstract: We introduce MORAD, an online reinforcement learning framework for backbone-conditioned RNA diffusion models that trains a single shared policy across diverse target backbones. Structure-conditioned RNA inverse design seeks nucleotide sequences compatible with a target three-dimensional backbone, yet existing reinforcement learning approaches either optimize a separate policy for each target backbone or rely on offline preference optimization, leaving online post-training of a reusable backbone-conditioned model largely unexplored. MORAD combines backbone-conditioned group sampling, group-relative reward normalization, and a forward-process diffusion objective. Beyond existing RL rewards that primarily target tertiary structural quality, MORAD jointly optimizes six measurements spanning tertiary geometry, base pairing, ensemble behavior, and sequence composition. To aggregate these heterogeneous objectives despite differences in scale and optimization direction, MORAD maps each measurement to a bounded desirability score and combines them with a weighted geometric mean. Compared with a tertiary-structure-only reward, this multi-objective formulation improves 10 of the 11 evaluation metrics that have a preferred direction. Applied to pretrained RIDE, MORAD improves GDT-TS by 16.0% (from 0.3300 to 0.3827) and pairing MCC by 19.4% (from 0.6110 to 0.7295), while reducing normalized ensemble defect by 27.5% (from 0.3906 to 0.2830). On the test set, MORAD outperforms RiboDiffusion, gRNAde, and RDesign across tertiary structural accuracy, secondary-structure pairing, and thermodynamic quality, establishing a new state of the art in structure-conditioned RNA inverse design.

title: Vocal Intensity Conversion with Continuous SPL Control via Adversarial Training
abstract: Vocal intensity conversion renders a recorded utterance at a different vocal intensity, rather than simply scaling its amplitude, while preserving its content and speaker identity. Existing systems control intensity through a reference utterance or a few discrete categories. Instead, we control the conversion with any target sound pressure level (SPL) on a continuous dB scale. A lightweight converter, trained as a conditional cycle-consistent GAN without parallel data, transforms the features of a frozen speech encoder, from which a pretrained vocoder resynthesizes the speech. We compare three representations, log-mel spectrograms, WavLM, and SpeechTokenizer, and introduce an objective protocol that measures the achieved intensity change against the target one on a calibrated corpus. With WavLM, the converter achieves a measured 83% of the target change in intensity and also shifts the fundamental frequency. A perceptual evaluation confirms that perceived vocal intensity increases with the target level on amplitude-normalized stimuli.

evidence.abstract: Vocal intensity conversion renders a recorded utterance at a different vocal intensity, rather than simply scaling its amplitude, while preserving its content and speaker identity. title: Lower Bounds for Randomized Linear-Oracle Optimization over Strongly Convex Sets
abstract: Recent results [arXiv:2602.04378, arXiv:2602.22608] have established worst-case objective-error lower bounds of order $1/T^2$ after $T$ linear minimization oracle (LMO) calls, matching the upper bound [arXiv:1406.1305] in its dependence on $T$ and thereby resolving a long-standing open question. Upon close inspection, however, both lower bounds are somewhat brittle. The first [arXiv:2602.04378] applies only to the standard Frank--Wolfe algorithm, and, as we show, its prescribed slow exact-line-search trajectories can amplify sufficiently small initialization errors exponentially, corresponding to roughly one additional bit of initialization accuracy per iteration. The second [arXiv:2602.22608] obtains lower bounds for any deterministic LMO-based first-order method via a resisting oracle that adversarially adapts to the queries of the algorithm. In both cases it is conceivable that randomization may circumvent these lower bounds; in particular, neither establishes a lower bound for unrestricted randomized first-order LMO methods. We close this gap by proving an $Ω(L\operatorname{diam}(S)^2/T^2)$ distributional lower bound for randomized first-order linear minimization oracle methods over strongly convex sets. While our construction reuses the family of [arXiv:2602.22608], our proof characterizes the conditional distribution of the hidden permutation after adaptive queries and bounds the expected decrease of a combinatorial statistic controlling optimizer variance. We further show that the same error threshold holds with probability at least $3/4$ and yields a stopping-time tail bound.

title: Supplementary Material: Detection of Cyberbullying Roles Through Supervised NLP in Adolescents’ Written Narratives
abstract: This project hosts the supplementary material for the article “Detection of Cyberbullying Roles Through Supervised Natural Language Processing in Adolescents’ Written Narratives”. The study developed and evaluated supervised NLP models to detect involvement in cyberbullying and the roles of cyberbystander, cybervictim, and cyberperpetrator, using school narratives written by Spanish adolescents (N = 2,655). The project contains two files: Supplementary Table S1: performance of all fine-tuned transformer models (BETO, DistilBETO, RoBERTa-bne, and BERTin; long text, short text, and mix) for each role. Supplementary Table S2: performance of all hybrid models (transformer [CLS] embeddings with a class-weighted ensemble classifier), across backbones, text types, and all combinations of auxiliary variables (age, sex, and grade), including the configuration without demographic variables. Metrics reported are F1, ROC-AUC, precision, recall, specificity, and Test Index (see the article for its definition). The raw texts are not shared, to protect the privacy of the participants (minors).

title: CUSTOMER AI INVOLVEMENT AND TOURISM EXPERIENCE VALUE: THE MEDIATING ROLE OF CUSTOMER INTERACTION
abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies is reshaping tourism service environments and transforming how tourists participate in tourism experiences. Drawing on the perspective of service-dominant logic, this study examines how Customer AI involvement influences tourism experience value in smart tourism contexts and explores the mediating role of customer interaction. Data were collected through an online survey of tourists with recent travel experiences, resulting in 264 valid responses. Confirmatory factor analysis and hierarchical regression analysis were conducted to test the proposed hypotheses. The results show that Customer AI involvement has a significant positive effect on tourism experience value. In addition, interpersonal interaction significantly mediates the relationship between Customer AI involvement and tourism experience value, whereas the mediating role of emotional interaction is not supported. These findings suggest that tourists’ engagement with AI technologies can enhance tourism experience value, partly through facilitating interpersonal communication and information exchange during tourism experiences. The study contributes to the literature by introducing the concept of Customer AI involvement into tourism experience research and by examining customer interaction as a multidimensional mechanism in AI-enabled tourism environments. The findings also provide practical implications for tourism enterprises seeking to enhance tourism experiences through the effective application of intelligent technologies.

title: Rooftop photovoltaic potential in data-scarce regions using open-source geospatial information: Scenario-based approach for a Mediterranean coastal city
abstract: Rooftop photovoltaic (PV) systems can support urban decarbonization, yet data scarcity limits city-scale assessments in developing regions. This study develops an open-source 2D GIS workflow for five central districts of Antalya, Turkiye, using Overture Maps building footprints. A three-stage procedure combined spatial and size filters, geometry and land-use screening, and targeted image inspection to retain the continuous urban building stock while excluding rural settlements, greenhouses, and structures smaller than 60 m 2 . Planimetric agreement was evaluated against 60 manually delineated reference structures totaling 93,070 m 2 . Structure-level mean absolute percentage error was 8.48%, whereas total-area relative error was 0.13%; leave-one-out values ranged from −0.43% to +0.96%, demonstrating sensitivity to sample composition. After screening, 130,458 structures with 38.97 million m 2 of gross rooftop footprint remained. Because verified building-use labels and citywide 3D height data were unavailable, rooftop availability was represented by literature-supported utilization factors of 0.20 and 0.50, incorporating obstructions, access, setbacks, layout constraints, and inter-row spacing. With annual plane-of-array irradiation of 2084.62 kWh m −2 , module efficiency of 21%, and a performance ratio of 0.75, technical generation was estimated at 2.56 to 6.40 TWh yr −1 . Under an average-grid displacement factor of 0.430 tCO₂ MWh −1 , this corresponds to 1.10 to 2.75 MtCO₂ yr −1 . These estimates represent screening-level technical potential, not building-specific deployment forecasts, because source-data omissions, inter-building shading, structural suitability, permitting, and grid constraints remain unresolved. The workflow separates footprint error, preprocessing decisions, and rooftop-utilization uncertainty, providing a transparent screening framework for data-scarce cities.

title: DICE: Tilting the Odds through Interface Attackson System One Model
abstract: System One models offer typed judgments that applications can turn into decisions. Their answers, however, are conditional on the state and question supplied by surrounding components, and on how the application uses the response. We study this boundary in a Jev-based pipeline with bounded substitutions at three adapter outputs: state extraction, question generation, and output interpretation. Across three small synthetic studies, each adapter can change the final decision while Jev and its authentic API responses remain outside attacker control. The cases expose distinct failures of source fidelity, answer meaning, and response relevance. Checks that bind these relationships stopped the corresponding interventions we tested, although source verification also rejected some valid clean decisions. The pilot identifies where correct request-level judgments can lose their connection to the original task; it does not estimate the prevalence of these failures in deployed systems.

title: VETNET: Assembling Benchmark Datasets for AI-Driven Veterinary Innovation
abstract: VETNET represents an ecosystem of live benchmark datasets and evaluation frameworks designed to accelerate AI-driven innovation in animal science and veterinary medicine through standardized, high-quality datasets and multi-institutional collaboration across academic and non-academic sectors. This framework addresses the gap between AI advances in human medicine and the fragmented state of veterinary AI development.

title: Neural Surrogate Modeling of Ultrasonic Wave Propagation in Heterogeneous Media
abstract: Neural surrogates provide computationally efficient auto-regressive modeling of wave propagation, enabling e.g. fast inverse solutions. Despite recent progress, the current surrogates are not yet sufficient for the needs of ultrasonic sensing, characterized by high frequency and heterogeneous propagation media. We show how methods building on Fourier Neural Operators (FNO) fail to capture essential signal features, such as reflections, whereas U-Net -based methods learn the wave fields well but lack the ability to transfer information across different spatial scales. We then propose a new surrogate that captures the best of the two worlds, by integrating FNOs and local-integral resampling into a U-Net architecture. We show it can be trained on limited data, and that the predictions are robust to input noise and work across spatial scales.

title: Conditional Indexing Lower Bounds and Normalization Boundaries for Elastic Subsequence Matching
abstract: We study static indexes for exact subsequence matching over all equal-length windows of a time series. Under deterministic SETH, for every fixed $β\ge1$ and $δ\in(0,1)$, we exclude $O(N^β)$ preprocessing together with $O(N^{1-δ})$ worst-case query time on domains containing the reduction's polylogarithmic query lengths. The bounded-error counterpart assumes randomized SETH. The results cover specified warping, bottleneck, edit, subsequence, local-alignment, and complexity-adjusted scores. Their reductions share a data-independent query interface but require different arguments for all-window soundness. We give complete representative proofs for the distinct mechanisms and state the changes needed by related scores. For soft-DTW, integer scaling yields an exact Boolean-predicate reduction in Word-RAM; a model with exact transcendental primitives requires a separate assumption. For independent window-wise Z-normalization, balanced coordinate gadgets and shifted-window moment bounds yield exact lower bounds for squared-cost DTW and discrete Fréchet distance. We give finite-word comparisons and a specified length-dependent rounding rule preserving these gaps. Raw and normalized discrete Fréchet constructions also exclude feasible-solution approximation within any fixed factor below two. Finally, we prove conditional signal-attenuation bounds for normalized anchor constructions and a fast index under the all-window common-mean promise.

title: Compactness and Noncompactness for the Positive Yamabe--Escobar Problem with Minimal Boundary
abstract: We study the Yamabe--Escobar equation prescribing positive constant scalar curvature and minimal boundary. The compactness conjecture asks whether being conformally equivalent to the round hemisphere is the only obstruction for its set of positive solutions to be compact. In this paper we show that this is true for dimensions 3leq nleq 14. We show that this dimensional threshold n_*=14 is sharp by constructing in ngeq 15 nonumbilic and non-locally-conformally-flat examples of metrics in the hemisphere for which a noncompact sequence of solutions exists. We do the same for the special classes of locally conformally flat metrics, n_*^{LCF}=18, and the metrics with umbilic boundary, n_*^{umb} =20. In all three settings we also prove that the Weyl--umbilicity vanishing conjecture holds for 4leq nleq n_* and construct counterexamples in n>n_* by perturbing the noncompactness examples. To the best of the author's knowledge, these are the first locally conformally flat noncompactness constructions for the positive-scalar-curvature, minimal-boundary case of the Yamabe--Escobar equation, outside the conformal class of the round hemisphere.

title: Scaling RNA Foundation Models through Iterative Refinement
abstract: Biological function in RNA is encoded across scales, from local sequence motifs to long-range structural dependencies. Conventional RNA foundation models couple parameter capacity and inference depth within a fixed architecture, prescribing a fixed computation graph for each inference. Here we present Eco-RNA, an 80M-parameter RNA foundation model that makes inference depth adjustable through learned iterative refinement. Its shared, input-conditioned Transformer core refines sequence representations through repeated application. The iteration count is selected after training and controls effective depth at fixed model parameters. We train across recurrent depths with masked reconstruction, state regularization, and a one-sided loss that anchors deeper reconstruction to a shallow reference. On the 70-assay RNAGym fitness benchmark, increasing refinement from one to four iterations raises aggregate absolute Spearman correlation from 0.242 to 0.286, with the gain retained through eight iterations. At four iterations, Eco-RNA surpasses the current SOTA Evo 2 40B on all three aggregate fitness metrics despite 500x fewer parameters. Its iteration configurations advance the compute-performance Pareto frontier among the evaluated models. It also outperforms the evaluated baselines in non-coding RNA family classification, RNA secondary-structure prediction, and chemical probing profile prediction. These results establish internal inference computation as an effective scaling dimension for RNA foundation models.

title: AD-SRF: Attack-Defense Semantic Reinforcement for Multi-Modal Image Fusion
abstract: Existing image fusion methods struggle to balance visual quality and semantic attributes due to the inherent conflict between their optimization objectives. To address this challenge, we propose an attack-defense semantic reinforcement framework for multi-modal image fusion, termed AD-SRF. By decoupling the optimization of these two aspects and then losslessly reintegrating them, this framework injects rich semantic attributes into the fused image without compromising its visual quality. First, we develop a transformer-based restorative visual fusion network as a strong visual baseline. Equipped with the cross-modal retrieval module and the information restoration-fusion collaborative loss, it produces highly visible fused images even under degraded conditions. Second, we introduce an attack-defense game mechanism to strengthen the semantic attributes of the fused images. The attacker learns perturbation patterns that impair downstream segmentation, whereas the defender restores missing semantics from the original inputs and reintegrates them into the fused image through an imperceptible semantic map. Through iterative adversarial interaction, this mechanism drives the defender to continually strengthen the fused image's semantic attributes, boosting downstream segmentation performance without compromising visual quality. Extensive experiments demonstrate that AD-SRF achieves a win-win performance in both visual quality and semantic attributes. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/HaoZhang1018/AD-SRF.

title: Neural networks are more modular than single neurons suggest
abstract: Neural networks routinely develop representations in which individual neurons contribute to multiple distinct functions, leading to the widespread view that such networks lack modular organization. We challenge this conclusion by introducing a formally nested hierarchy of modularity: unit-level, which requires distinct computations to occupy disjoint neurons; orthogonal, which asks whether a rotation reveals functionally independent subspaces; and linear, which asks whether a bounded linear map can separate task-relevant computations into independent subspaces. We develop a unified framework for learning decompositions at each level and evaluating them causally through selective ablation. Across vision models, language models and multi-task Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), we find that networks which lack unit-level modularity nonetheless often exhibit clear functional modularity at the subspace level. In vision and language models, content versus style and syntax versus semantics respectively dissociate under subspace ablation despite sharing overlapping populations of neurons. These learned subspaces also align differentially with brain data, with content and style subspaces predicting higher and lower visual cortex respectively, and semantic subspaces outperforming syntactic ones in predicting language cortex activity. In RNNs trained on multiple cognitive tasks and previously shown to lack modular structure, our decomposition recovers sharp double dissociations between tasks. The absence of unit-level modularity frequently coexists with clear subspace-level modularity across domains, enabling targeted intervention on specific computations even in networks where no individual neuron is specialized, with broad implications for mechanistic interpretability and for understanding functional organization in both biological and artificial neural systems.

title: PAGE: Parts-Aware Guidance for Co-Speech Gesture Portrait Video Generation
abstract: Co-speech gesture video generation aims to synthesize realistic, audio-driven portrait videos from a single reference image and a speech signal. Despite advances in visual quality, diffusion-based approaches still suffer from degraded local details and imperfect audio-visual alignment. We present PAGE (Parts-Aware GuidancE), a general, backbone-agnostic optimization framework for diffusion-based generation that enhances local spatial fidelity and global audio-visual consistency at both the training-objective and denoising-trajectory levels. During training, we propose Parts-Specific Reweighting (PSR), which adaptively increases supervision in semantically important regions such as lips, eyes, and hands, improving visual fidelity in perceptually critical areas. During inference, we introduce Consistency Classifier Guidance (CCG), an audio-conditioned latent classifier that identifies and corrects audio-visual inconsistencies in the generated video. We further design Differential Guidance (DG), an efficient inference strategy that refines facial and body motion separately while avoiding cross-region interference. To enable large-scale evaluation, we construct the Chinese Announcer Speech (CAS) dataset, the first comprehensive Chinese benchmark for co-speech gesture portrait video generation. Compared with the widely used PATS dataset, CAS includes substantially more identities, video clips, and scene diversity. Extensive experiments on both PATS and CAS demonstrate that PAGE achieves state-of-the-art performance in perceptual quality, gesture diversity, and audio-visual alignment. Project page: https://aigc-explorer.github.io/PAGE/.

title: Sonic-AMG: Streaming Human Motion Generation from Spatial Audio
abstract: Modeling human reactions to spatial audio requires understanding both what is heard and where it comes from. Prior work generates motion offline from complete acoustic and spatial input sequences. Humans, however, react to sounds without knowing what they will hear next. We present Sonic-AMG, to our knowledge the first framework for streaming human motion generation from spatial audio. The model encodes acoustic content and body-relative source geometry as separate tokens. Conditioned on these tokens, a causal transformer with a flow head generates continuous motion latents, from which a causal decoder reconstructs motion segments. Standard teacher-forced training derives motion histories and body-relative source locations from ground-truth motion, whereas streaming inference relies on generated motion for both, resulting in a training-inference mismatch. To reduce this history discrepancy, we introduce rehearsal training, which combines full-sequence teacher-forced supervision with supervised prediction along short autoregressive self-rollouts. To keep spatial conditioning consistent with generated motion, we propose spatial feedback, which recomputes body-relative source locations from generated root poses during both rehearsal training and inference. On SAM, Sonic-AMG achieves state-of-the-art FID and R-precision. It further supports real-time online generation of coherent reactions across sound events and source locations. Project page: https://jingchengni.com/sonic-amg/.
