title: Integrasi Metode VCIRS Dengan Teori Certainty Factor Pada Sistem Pakar Screening Awal Gangguan Tidur Pada Orang Dewasa
abstract: Gangguan tidur merupakan masalah kesehatan yang signifikan di kalangan orang dewasa dengan prevalensi tinggi di Indonesia, namun sebagian besar kasusnya tidak terdeteksi karena adanya normalisasi gejala oleh masyarakat. Kurangnya screening awal menghambat penanganan efektif dan meningkatkan risiko penyakit kronis serta penurunan produktivitas. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengembangkan sebuah sistem pakar berbasis website untuk screening awal gangguan tidur pada orang dewasa dengan mengintegrasikan metode Variable-Centered Intelligent Rule System (VCIRS) dan teori Certainty Factor (CF). Metode VCIRS digunakan untuk proses akuisisi pengetahuan dan inferensi berbasis aturan yang efisien, sedangkan Certainty Factor diterapkan untuk mengelola ketidakpastian pada gejala subjektif guna memberikan tingkat keyakinan pada hasil screening. Metode pengembangan sistem dilakukan melalui tahap pengumpulan data gejala dari pakar, pemodelan aturan dengan VCIRS, dan perhitungan bobot kepastian menggunakan CF. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa sistem pakar yang dikembangkan berhasil mengimplementasikan kedua metode tersebut untuk mengenali kecenderungan gangguan tidur secara mandiri. Berdasarkan pengujian yang dilakukan, sistem ini terbukti sangat efektif dan andal dengan hasil pengujian Black Box menunjukkan tingkat fungsionalitas 100%. Selain itu, sistem mencapai tingkat akurasi sebesar 96,15% jika dibandingkan dengan data diagnosa pakar (psikolog). Dengan demikian, sistem ini dapat digunakan sebagai alat bantu deteksi dini yang akurat untuk meningkatkan kesadaran kesehatan tidur pengguna sebelum melakukan konsultasi lebih lanjut dengan tenaga profesional. Kata kunci: Sistem Pakar, Gangguan Tidur, Screening Awal, VCIRS, Certainty Factor

title: Метод автоматизованого виявлення структурних невідповідностей в університетських лекційних курсах на основі часового графа знань
abstract: Університетські курси мають послідовну структуру: кожна лекція спирається на поняття, введені раніше. Коли такі курси оновлюються або збираються з різних джерел, у них накопичуються структурні невідповідності. Такі невідповідності важко виявити вручну, тому їх автоматизоване виявлення є актуальним завданням. Метою дослідження є підвищення точності та повноти автоматизованого виявлення таких невідповідностей порівняно з прямим запитом до великої мовної моделі. Об’єктом дослідження є процес автоматизованого виявлення структурних невідповідностей у послідовності лекцій курсу, предметом – моделі та методи, що його реалізують. Наукова новизна полягає в методі, який поєднує вилучення понять і відношень передумов великою мовною моделлю з часовим графом знань, вузли якого зберігають порядок введення понять. Завдяки цьому чотири види невідповідностей стають розв’язними графовими алгоритмами: використання до введення, порушення порядку передумов, конфлікт визначень і поняття без визначення. На відміну від розглянутих рішень, які аналізують узгодженість між курсами освітньої програми або будують освітні графи знань для навігації, метод перевіряє лекції окремого курсу. Метод реалізовано як конвеєр із чотирьох етапів: сегментація, вилучення, ототожнення сутностей і виявлення. Його оцінено на трьох україномовних університетських курсах з архітектури програмного забезпечення, педагогіки та дискретної математики. Повноту виміряно на 81 контрольованій ін’єкції дефектів. Точність виміряно на 161 природній позначці, оціненій одним анотатором. Метод досягає повноти 0,96 проти 0,78 у прямого запиту. Його макроусереднена точність становить 0,82 проти 0,62, і він підтверджує 123 справжні дефекти проти 14. Обмеженнями дослідження є одна мова матеріалів, один анотатор і точність, що падає до 0,59 на тексті зі щільною математичною нотацією.

title: LLM fine-tuning for international news style generation and cross-cultural dissemination quality assessment
abstract: The rapid globalization of news media has heightened the demand for high-quality, culturally adapted international news content. However, generating news articles that faithfully conform to the stylistic conventions of diverse national media outlets while maintaining cross-cultural semantic fidelity remains a formidable challenge. This paper presents a novel framework that leverages fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) for international news style generation and introduces a comprehensive cross-cultural dissemination quality assessment (CDQA) methodology. Specifically, we construct a multilingual international news corpus spanning seven major languages and ten distinct journalistic style profiles, drawn from leading international media organizations. We then apply parameter-efficient fine-tuning via Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) on a LLaMA-2-based backbone, augmented with a style-aware prefix adapter that conditions generation on target-style embeddings. For quality assessment, we propose a multi-dimensional evaluation framework integrating automatic metrics—including BLEU-4, ROUGE-L, and BERTScore—with a novel Cross-Cultural Appropriateness Score (CCAS) grounded in culturological theory. Experimental results demonstrate that our fine-tuned model achieves a BLEU-4 score of 42.7 and a BERTScore F1 of 0.876 on held-out test sets, outperforming strong baselines by 5.3 and 3.1 percentage points, respectively. Human evaluation conducted by bilingual journalists across five language pairs yields mean fluency and cultural appropriateness ratings of 4.21/5.00 and 4.08/5.00, respectively. Cross-cultural quality classification accuracy reaches 87.3%, validating the effectiveness of the CCAS framework. This work offers a scalable, reproducible pipeline for high-fidelity international news generation, with direct implications for global media localization.

title: SplatQ: Interaction-Aware Pruning of 3D Gaussian Splatting via Quadratic Selection
abstract: Existing 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) pruning methods primarily rely on global Top-K selection based on independent importance scores, lacking regional budget control and ignoring joint deletion effects. Consequently, they cannot ensure balanced reconstruction quality across a scene. We propose SplatQ, a combinatorial pruning algorithm that coordinates regional budget allocation and joint Gaussian selection under a fixed budget. SplatQ partitions Gaussians by spatial proximity and appearance similarity into size-limited blocks, decomposing global selection into subproblems of a specific size. It then smooths importance-based block retention quotas to prevent excessive budget concentration. Finally, it constructs a quadratic approximation of joint deletion effects using the responses of representative pixel colors to changes in Gaussian opacity. Individual responses, pairwise interactions, and quota penalties are incorporated into a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) objective, solved using simulated annealing (SA) or a coherent Ising machine (CIM) to jointly select Gaussians. Experiments on 5 benchmarks demonstrate that SplatQ outperforms state-of-the-art pruning methods in aggregate reconstruction quality, spatial quality balance, and rendering speed. Ablations confirm that budget smoothing improves local detail reconstruction, while interaction modeling improves Gaussian selection quality under a fixed budget.

evidence.title: SplatQ: Interaction-Aware Pruning of 3D Gaussian Splatting via Quadratic Selection
evidence.abstract: Existing 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) pruning methods primarily rely on global Top-K selection based on independent importance scores, lacking regional budget control and ignoring joint deletion effects. Consequently, they cannot ensure balanced reconstruction quality across a scene. We propose SplatQ, a combinatorial pruning algorithm that coordinates regional budget allocation and joint Gaussian selection under a fixed budget. SplatQ partitions Gaussians by spatial proximity and appearance similarity into size-limited blocks, decomposing global selection into subproblems of a specific size. It then smooths importance-based block retention quotas to prevent excessive budget concentration. Finally, it constructs a quadratic approximation of joint deletion effects using the responses of representative pixel colors to changes in Gaussian opacity. Individual responses, pairwise interactions, and quota penalties are incorporated into a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) objective, solved using simulated annealing (SA) or a coherent Ising machine (CIM) to jointly select Gaussians. Experiments on 5 benchmarks demonstrate that SplatQ outperforms state-of-the-art pruning methods in aggregate reconstruction quality, spatial quality balance, and rendering speed. Ablations confirm that budget smoothing improves local detail reconstruction, while interaction modeling improves Gaussian selection quality under a fixed budget.

title: Grounded-Dreamer: Robot Learning from World Model Synthetic Data with Physical Grounding
abstract: Scaling robot manipulation policies requires large amounts of diverse, action-labeled data, yet collecting such data in the real world remains expensive and difficult to scale. Existing methods either depend on human teleoperation, rely on simulation with limited visual realism, or use human videos that lack embodiment-specific annotations. In this paper, we introduce Grounded-Dreamer, a framework for synthesizing physically grounded robot manipulation data with video world models while avoiding human teleoperation demonstrations. Grounded-Dreamer combines the visual realism of generative video models with simulator physics engines. Starting from a small set of real images depicting robot task initial states, our method automatically reconstructs task-relevant objects and camera geometry, aligns them in simulation, and collects physically valid trajectories. These trajectories are used to post-train both a video world model and an inverse dynamics model, enabling the generation of visually realistic robot manipulation videos and corresponding robot actions from real images. To filter physically implausible rollouts, Grounded-Dreamer replays generated trajectories in the reconstructed simulation and retains only those that successfully complete the tasks. The real-world robot policies are trained solely on the grounded synthetic trajectories without any human demonstrations. Empirical results in real-world tasks demonstrate that Grounded-Dreamer can synthesize physically grounded data and substantially facilitate policy learning without requiring human teleoperation effort.

title: FlyHack: Stress-Testing Mechanistic Claims in a Connectome-Constrained Visual Model
abstract: Connectome-constrained neural networks make biological components directly accessible to intervention, but their mechanistic conclusions can still depend on the comparison model, intervention, circuit representation and trained solution. We stress-test these dependencies in flyvis, a \emph{Drosophila} motion-vision model, using its 50-model ensemble, task-matched causal CNN controls and replicated interventions. At the level of model behaviour, three-level reverse-phi reversal in flyvis is strongly period- and velocity-dependent and also appears in task-matched CNNs; neither family reproduces the fly's stationary-sawtooth response. Adversarial direction reversal requires a perturbation bound of 0.21--0.27 times stimulus contrast in flyvis versus 0.13--0.25 in CNNs, but the gap over a parameter-matched CNN largely closes for larger CNNs. At the level of mechanism, matching attribution to the intervention matters: for held-out-mean replacement, first-order edge attribution patching reaches pooled AUROC 0.970 and Spearman 0.872, versus 0.933 and 0.126 when its zero-aligned score is evaluated against the same ground truth. Circuit conclusions also vary with representation and ensemble member. Greedy cell-type sets meet a model-relative T4/T5 tuning criterion in 25 of 50 models, while T4/T5 output silencing reduces the tested optic-flow behaviour to at most two of eight clips in 40. In six models where the cell-type search first succeeds, the corresponding connection sets can be pruned to 13--31 added classes; under an additional two-sided response-amplitude check, only two of those six first-success cell-type sets still meet the tuning threshold. These results support a narrower use of connectome-constrained models: they make mechanistic hypotheses directly testable, but the resulting claims must be scoped to the model family, intervention, representation and trained solution.

title: Training User Simulators with Latent Intrinsic Feedback
abstract: User simulators are gaining attention as environments to train LLM assistants that can better cope with the nuances of multi-turn conversations with real users. Prior work on user simulation has emphasized generating realistic user utterances, leaving unexplored their potential as a source of direct feedback on the assistant's responses. Such evaluation signals may not be explicitly communicated in language, but can instead reside in the latent reasoning of users. In this work, we introduce user simulators with intrinsic feedback, namely, models equipped with latent evaluation states: internal thoughts, reactions, and scalar ratings that evaluate the assistant from a first-person user perspective at each conversation turn. We train LLM-based simulators using interaction logs between real users and assistants and demonstrate that intrinsic feedback improves simulation realism and critiquing behaviors versus prompted simulator baselines, while also providing turn-level evaluations that existing fine-tuned simulators lack. Further, evaluations generated by our trained simulators correlate better with human judgments than those of prompted simulators of the same size. Lastly, our experiments reveal that simulators with intrinsic feedback provide effective reward signals for multi-turn RL training, matching setups that rely on external judge LLMs for rewards while cutting RL compute by more than half.

title: CoBe: A Benchmark For Conversational Counterfactual Text Editing
abstract: Counterfactual text editing is the ability to revise a given text in light of a hypothetical change while preserving facts not causally affected by that change. When asked what would have happened if a doctor had not recommended surgery, the model output should retain the patient's medical history and modify only the consequences of the decision. This requires causal understanding: a model must determine, without being explicitly instructed to, what events are affected by the hypothetical change and what should remain fixed. This skill is central to human reasoning, especially in safety-critical domains like healthcare or law. By contrast, the task of associational text generation merely generates text statistically associated with the altered condition. In the medical example, an associational response might make the patient's symptoms less severe because milder cases correlate with no surgery. Such responses produce a plausible scenario, but not the counterfactual version of the given one. Prior counterfactual-text datasets do not clearly separate these modes of reasoning. We introduce the Counterfactual Benchmark (CoBe), a testbed for models' zero-shot ability to counterfactually edit a given textual scenario when prompted to do so in a conversationally natural way. CoBe contains 2000 questions spanning healthcare, science and engineering, business, and everyday scenarios. We test a suite of frontier and smaller models, with frontier systems achieving an average score of $58.05\%$. Our findings indicate that models frequently default to associational generation rather than preserving the causal structure of the original scenario. Moreover, performance does not scale consistently with either model size or output token length, suggesting that the failure may reflect model training objectives rather than insufficient model capacity.

title: LongHarness: Advancing Agentic Reasoning over 100M-Token Corpora via Stateful Evidence Management
abstract: Corpus-level long-context reasoning requires agents to acquire and integrate evidence across document collections that exceed their context windows. Existing agent harnesses enable incremental access to these corpora, but acquired evidence and evolving conclusions often remain entangled in a growing interaction history. This implicit state management can lead to two coupled failure modes: unbounded exploration, where retrieval expands the interaction history without resolving decision-relevant information gaps, and evidence-state drift, where previously acquired evidence or subsequent corrections fail to inform the current conclusion. We present LongHarness, a model-agnostic harness that makes the interaction between acquired evidence and evolving conclusions explicit. Its core mechanism, Evidence-Conclusion Coevolution, uses unresolved conclusions to guide exploration toward missing information, while newly acquired evidence strengthens or revises the conclusions that directed the search. LongHarness couples this process with Evidence Lifecycle Management, which keeps accumulated evidence current and traceable throughout the interaction. Together, these mechanisms focus retrieval on remaining information needs and keep conclusions aligned with current evidence. We evaluate LongHarness on OfficeQA Pro V1 and V2, AA-LCR, and LongBench v2 using GLM-5.3-Flash and Qwen3.8-Flash. Compared with direct reasoning using the same backbone, LongHarness improves GLM-5.3-Flash exact match on OfficeQA Pro from 15.8% to 60.2% on V1 and from 4.4% to 61.1% on V2. Against state-of-the-art agent harnesses, it surpasses Claude Code by 12.0 percentage points on V1 and Codex by 18.9 points on V2. With Qwen3.8-Flash, LongHarness reaches 61.7% on V1, outperforming Claude Code by 8.3 points and Codex by 12.0 points.

title: Beyond Successful Robot Demonstrations: Learning from Human Interactions and Modeling Failure Dynamics
abstract: Action-conditioned world models offer a promising foundation for generalist robotic intelligence by predicting the consequences of actions. However, existing robotic datasets provide limited coverage of the diverse interaction dynamics required for generalizable world modeling. Large-scale egocentric human videos offer complementary interaction experience, yet the embodiment gap between human hands and robotic manipulators hinders effective cross-embodiment learning. Meanwhile, the predominance of successful demonstrations leaves failure dynamics substantially underrepresented, limiting the ability of world models to anticipate unsuccessful executions. To address these limitations, we introduce HF-WM, an action-conditioned world model that combines Human interaction learning with Failure-aware post-training. To bridge the embodiment gap, we develop a dual-branch framework that couples video generation with auxiliary pointflow prediction, using stabilized pointflow as a unified motion representation across human and robot interactions while suppressing egocentric camera motion. To improve failure modeling, we further perform Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) post-training on perturbed actions derived from successful demonstrations, guided by action alignment and physical plausibility rewards, enabling the model to learn plausible failure dynamics without paired ground-truth videos. Extensive experiments demonstrate that HF-WM achieves state-of-the-art performance in action-conditioned video generation and exhibits strong utility for policy evaluation in downstream robotic tasks.

title: Is Superintelligence the Final Form of Thought?
abstract: Could an artificial superintelligence create a form of thought that exceeds its own? This article examines changes in the concepts, representations, and inferences through which a system understands and formulates problems. Changes in code or architecture alone do not establish a cognitive transition. Existing accounts of intelligence amplification and quality superintelligence already allow for superior successors. The harder question is what would make their superiority a change of cognitive paradigm. I develop a provisional account of cognitive succession through three requirements: a creator's material contribution to forming its successor's resources, a consequential reorganization of those resources, and a sustained, transferable advantage under stated comparison conditions. Paradigmatic change matters because it alters the means through which further questions and learning become possible. Debates about conceptual acquisition and computational creativity clarify how richer resources might develop and how reorganization relates to search within a more general framework. Two thought experiments examine different changes: making learned relations available for further reasoning, and making the assumptions of inquiry open to assessment and revision. Contrasting developmental histories, a teaching comparison, and a proposed DreamCoder extension specify the evidence needed. A creator's later acquisition of its successor's resources can support an earlier transition even as the performance gap closes. The contribution is an explanatory relation within learning. Its future realization remains open: superiority to humans gives no reason to regard a form of thought as final.

title: From Retrieval to Evidence: A Task-Adaptive Two-Layer Knowledge Architecture for LLM Agents
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation and structured agent memory are commonly treated as competing ways to ground large language models. Our results show that their relative value changes with the task and that neither retrieved similarity nor graph association is sufficient evidence for an answer. We present a task-adaptive two-layer methodology combining a compact, reviewed knowledge layer for orientation and cross-source synthesis with a versioned evidence layer for exact lookup and claim support. A router selects the representation, while an independent admission stage checks named entities, time, source role, contradiction, and provenance. A controlled course-grounding study reveals a task-conditional crossover within Course 2: the distilled Body of Knowledge (BoK) trails plain RAG by 1.07 points on lookup and leads by 0.62 points on synthesis. Across a 72-question three-course lookup panel, RAG leads by 2.17 points; Course 1 synthesis is near parity. Complementary, position-debiased LLM-judged mastery comparisons favor the BoK on both courses. The standing representation is reduced 22–35-fold. An observational production case over a 289,642-chunk evidence base illustrates why candidate discovery, packet selection, and evidence admission require separate gates. The contribution is a tested method for assigning retrieval, structure, and evidence admission distinct responsibilities within one grounded agent architecture.

title: FedQDFU: Non-IID Federated Quantum Learning for Diabetic Foot Ulcer Classification from Deep Image Features
abstract: Diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) classification increasingly relies on learning frameworks that exploit medical image representations without centralizing raw data. This study presents FedQDFU, a feature-based federated quantum learning benchmark evaluating a compact variational quantum classifier (VQC) on deep features from VGG16, ResNet50, and DenseNet121, using frozen ImageNet-pretrained backbones as fixed feature extractors over 1020 samples from a single public DFU dataset (696 unique feature vectors after exact-duplicate auditing). Because patient identifiers are unavailable, duplicate-group-aware splitting prevents exact duplicates from crossing the development-test boundary but cannot guarantee patient-level independence. A 6-qubit VQC (43 parameters) is compared with a 129-parameter multilayer perceptron (MLP) under centralized learning, FedAvg, and FedProx across IID and Dirichlet non-IID client distributions (α∈{10,1,0.5,0.1}), with federated-compatible random projection, five-seed evaluation of the primary conditions, and bootstrap confidence intervals on a locked test set. At the primary non-IID setting (α=0.5), the VQC attains a lower mean Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) than the MLP on all three backbones (e.g., ResNet50: 0.782±0.011 vs. 0.650±0.041 under FedAvg); the paired bootstrap difference is significant only for ResNet50 at the uncorrected pairwise 95% level (ΔMCC=−0.115, 95% CI [−0.218,−0.016]), an effect a Bonferroni correction across backbones is estimated to remove, so this result should be read as suggestive rather than confirmed. No significant centralized-to-FedAvg VQC degradation is detected for any backbone, and a ResNet50 parameter-matched experiment shows the MLP-VQC gap persists even when the MLP is reduced to 41 parameters. Under severe non-IID heterogeneity (α=0.1), the seed-42 partition contains one entirely single-class client (mean pairwise Jensen–Shannon divergence 0.5653 vs. 0.1787 at α=0.5); federated aggregation of this degenerate update yields a fixed-threshold collapse in which all test samples are assigned the positive class (MCC = 0, sensitivity = 1, specificity = 0). This outcome is realization-dependent rather than deterministic: only one of five paired partition/training seeds reproduces the complete collapse.

title: Analysis of anomaly characteristics in mineralized segments using core drilling and geophysical logging
abstract: Reliable recognition of mineralized intervals from borehole logging data remains difficult because weak mineralization, thin layers, borehole disturbance, and lithological changes may produce similar curve responses. This study develops a multi-parameter coupled anomaly identification framework using density, resistivity, natural gamma, acoustic travel time, magnetic susceptibility, and polarizability logs acquired by the Kezuan Geophysical Logging Method. The framework integrates depth resampling, normalization, composite anomaly indexing, boundary-response calculation, anomaly-pattern matching, and lithology-constrained interval merging. Validation was performed using core records from Kezuan Well 1 and additional boreholes. In Well 1, 118 anomaly intervals were identified, of which 93 matched core-confirmed mineralized intervals, giving an accuracy of 78.8%, a false-negative rate of 20.3%, and a false-positive rate of 15.3%. The accuracy exceeded the single-parameter threshold method by 28.8 percentage points and the biparameter intersection method by 14.2 percentage points. External borehole validation produced accuracies of 75.4%–77.2%. The novelty of the framework lies in converting multi-parameter logging responses into boundary-constrained and geologically interpretable mineralized intervals rather than merely stacking abnormal curves. The results indicate that the method improves anomaly recognition under complex borehole conditions, although very thin and weakly mineralized zones remain difficult to detect.

title: Stride: Scale-Aware Multi-Agent Evolutionary Refinement for Infographic Generation
abstract: Infographic generation challenges text-to-image models because a single image must satisfy numerous visual, textual, and semantic constraints. Iterative agentic refinement with a multimodal verifier is a natural remedy, but existing methods face a scale mismatch: local edits cannot correct global composition errors, while full regeneration may destroy already-correct regions. We introduce Stride, a constraint-grounded multi-agent framework that treats refinement over any frozen generator as a history-aware evolution strategy. Stride separates constraint evaluation - whether each requirement is satisfied - from visual grounding - where and how it is violated. It then routes global revisions to a composer subagent and local corrections to a retoucher subagent. Each subagent conducts internal planning and generates multiple candidates, while Stride accepts a candidate only when it improves the verifier score, reducing regression across iterations. Because stochastic generators and imperfect verifiers make any single step unreliable, it is this combination of scale-aware routing, per-step redundancy, and monotonic acceptance that yields stable improvement across iterations. With fully open-weight generator-verifier systems, Stride outperforms proprietary systems including Nano-Banana-2.0 and Seedream-5.0-Pro on BizGenEval, matches GPT-Image-2.0 and surpasses Seedream-5.0-Pro on IGenBench, and achieves a new state-of-the-art score on WISE, while substantially outperforming existing agentic methods across all evaluated benchmarks.

title: Variance Fingerprints: Component-Wise Identification of Content Factors by Augmentation Design
abstract: Augmentation-based self-supervised learning can recover the content shared across views without separating its underlying factors into individual coordinates. We ask whether augmentations can be designed to make those factors identifiable. Our approach allows content factors to fluctuate across augmented views while preserving their mean for each source instance. Each instance receives a fixed, recorded set of augmentation strengths that controls how much its factors fluctuate. When factors respond differently to changes in these strengths, their patterns of variation provide information that distinguishes them. Under suitable decoder and support assumptions, we prove that these differences identify individual factors in a conditional Gaussian model, up to permutation, scaling, and translation. We then develop a learner that uses the recorded strengths to estimate these patterns jointly across instances, enabling learning from few views per instance. Synthetic experiments demonstrate near-perfect factor recovery through nonlinear mixing. Controlled dSprites experiments show improved coordinate alignment using augmentations that target known factors, even without telling the learner which augmentation corresponds to which representation coordinate. These results suggest a route to component identification in self-supervised learning: augmentation design can supply identifying information beyond shared content alone.

title: Do Prompt Optimizers Break Requirements They Are Not Scored On? A Preregistered Study
abstract: Prompt optimizers rewrite a prompt to raise one target metric, but prompts also state requirements the metric does not score, such as an output format, citations, or abstention. In a preregistered study, we run GEPA, MIPROv2, and TextGrad on HotpotQA, SQuAD 2.0, and IFEval and count per-item violations of unscored requirements with deterministic checks. By the preregistered criterion, all three optimizers produce regressions, substantially on HotpotQA, where net regression in citation validity reaches 10.7 to 41.6 points while exact match rises by 21 to 34 points. A post-hoc decomposition changes this reading. The optimized prompts elicit reasoning before the required JSON object, and under the 200-token output cap used throughout, 13.9% to 47.0% of responses end before any answer appears. Among parseable outputs, net regression is within 3 points of zero. With a 1,024-token cap, extraction failures disappear, content regression stays below 1 point, and exact match rises further. Two simple gates fail the preregistered criterion. The side effect is narrower than hypothesized: optimized prompts are more accurate and break an explicit output contract, and a lenient target metric does not show the cost.

title: Activation-Matched Gibbs Initialization for Neural Networks
abstract: Initialization plays an important role in neural network training. A classical way to address this task relies on Gaussian weights and preactivations, motivated in part by their analytical tractability and their emergence in large-width approximations. We propose an activation-induced initialization based on a statistical-mechanical viewpoint: for activations that arise as the gradient of a Legendre potential, the latter defines a Gibbs family of preactivation distributions. This perspective allows the preactivation distribution, rather than only its scale, to be adapted to the activation geometry.

title: Extremal same-basis correlations: full-rank rigidity and a stabilizer classification
abstract: Complete written proofs and two exact replayable checker implementations classify all full-Schmidt-rank equality states without assuming stabilizer structure, classify every two-qudit pure stabilizer score at odd prime dimension, and determine the sharp pure-state ratio p/2 for every prime p congruent to 1 modulo 4. The general rank-deficient equality classification and the sharp ratio for primes congruent to 3 modulo 4, p at least 7, remain open in this record. This is an independently authored preprint with AI-assisted research and self-audit, not external professional peer review or a priority claim. The fixed immutable GitHub Release is https://github.com/mxym/math/releases/tag/ecqc-extremal-classification-v1. AI-assisted research and writing; no external funding. Existing licenses and third-party notices are retained.

title: Semantic Segment Alignment and Granular ASR Performance Evaluation with Segment- and Word-Level WER
abstract: Word Error Rate (WER) is the de facto standard for evaluating automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems. Yet, conventional WER is a global average, which obscures critical performance variations across semantically important transcript segments; segment-level WER can reveal deeper insights for performance evaluation of ASR systems in many applications, and word-level WER can provide an additional perspective that can guide fine-tuning for ASR models. In this paper, we focus on segment- and word-level WER calculation. While it is possible to calculate these metrics using custom postprocessing scripts on top of existing tools such as SCTK/sclite, this approach has not been widely reported, likely due to limited application demand. Our work is motivated by ASR applications to air traffic control (ATC) communications, where safety-critical semantic segments—such as aircraft callsigns, action commands, and numerical values—demand prioritized performance monitoring. While evaluating the postprocessing-based approach, we also explored alternatives. Through systematic analysis of Levenshtein edit distance (LD) table patterns, we derive rules for aligning semantic segments in reference transcripts to corresponding hypothesis transcripts and computing localized—segment- and word-level—LD, used for evaluating local WER. Based on these rules, this paper introduces a comprehensive framework for segment alignment and segment- and word-level WER evaluation using dynamic programming algorithms that are markedly more efficient than postprocessing-based approaches using existing tools. We present three fast algorithms for segment alignment, as well as segment- and word-level LD calculations. To address accuracy issues caused by prefix drift (hallucination), we introduce refined implementations that mitigate this problem. For the word-level case, we introduce a generalized LD (GLD) with associated attribution rules that distribute shared blame to words potentially responsible for hallucinations. We validate the word-level GLD algorithm through simulation, where the ground-truth value for GLD attribution is obtained from perfect word-level transcript alignment established using simultaneously generated reference and hypothesis transcripts. All algorithms are implemented in an open-source Python tool called salwer, designed for voice-assisted avionics applications based on ATC voice instructions. The tool can be readily modified or extended to other domains requiring localized error evaluation. Experimental results demonstrate that segment- and word-level WER reveal critical insights hidden in global averages, particularly for high-risk words and segments. Analysis results based on our framework enable fine-grained ASR performance assessment and support targeted model improvements.

title: AI-Based Prognostic Risk Stratification of Adult-Type Diffuse Glioma Patients from H&E-Stained Slides
abstract: Background/Objectives: Adult-type diffuse gliomas (ADGs) are aggressive brain tumors with highly variable clinical outcomes. Prognostic assessment directly from routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained whole-slide images (WSIs) could support personalized decision-making. Methods: To our knowledge, this is the first systematic benchmarking of pathology foundation models (FMs) and multiple instance learning (MIL) methods for overall survival (OS) risk stratification in ADGs under the 2021 World Health Organization (WHO) classification. A retrospective, multi-institutional cohort of 817 subjects from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) was analyzed. Following tissue segmentation and patch-level curation, we evaluated 77 pathology FM-MIL combinations (11 FMs × 7 MIL methods), together with seven ResNet-50 baseline configurations (84 encoder-MIL configurations in total), using patient-level 10-fold cross-validation. A perturbation-based evaluation assessed attention mechanism faithfulness. Results: UNI2 paired with MambaMIL achieved the highest cross-validated concordance index (C-index = 0.77), whereas its time-dependent AUC was modest (0.60–0.61 at 12–36 months), and several combinations performed comparably. Kaplan–Meier analysis demonstrated significant separation between high- and low-risk groups (log-rank p = 9.16 × 10−17; hazard ratio [HR] = 2.90, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.23–3.76), with a median OS of 16.6 months (95% CI: 15.0–20.4) versus 63.5 months (95% CI: 43.9-NR), respectively. Tertile stratification confirmed a monotonic OS gradient from 94.5 months to 14.7 months (p = 3.25 × 10−17). Risk stratification within individual WHO 2021 types was not significant. Most domain-specific FMs outperformed the ImageNet-pretrained baseline, and the removal of highly attended patches reduced performance, supporting attention faithfulness. Conclusions: The AI-derived risk score remained associated with OS after adjustment for individual clinical and molecular variables, but independent prognostic value was not demonstrated in the fully adjusted model (HR = 1.32, 95% CI: 0.94–1.85, p = 0.104), and its discrimination largely reflects differences between WHO 2021 types. This benchmarking framework provides guidance for FM-MIL design in computational pathology applications targeting survival prediction; external validation is required before clinical application.

title: PARM: Passage-Anchored Relation-Aware Multi-Hop Retrieval for Evidence-Grounded Question Answering
abstract: Multi-hop question answering requires discovering interconnected facts from distributed text passages and entity relations, and constructing complete evidence chains to support the final answer. Existing graph-based retrieval-augmented generation approaches often rely on limited initial retrieval seeds or semantic anchors for graph expansion, making evidence discovery sensitive to anchor coverage, candidate generation strategies, and early filtering decisions. To address these challenges, we propose PARM, a graph retrieval framework that introduces passage-level evidence anchors before graph reasoning. Specifically, PARM first identifies relevant passages through lexical retrieval and semantic reranking, and then combines question entities with passage-linked entities to construct complementary graph search anchors. A bounded multi-hop graph search is subsequently performed to generate explicit relation paths under predefined hop and path budgets. The generated paths are further ranked by jointly modeling semantic relevance, question–relation compatibility, and graph structural information. Finally, the selected passages, relation paths, and provenance information are organized into a traceable evidence package for answer generation. Extensive experiments are conducted on the MuSiQue and 2WikiMultiHopQA benchmarks. Across three fixed 1000-question subsets of 2WikiMultiHopQA, PARM increases the mean EM score from 0.3403 to 0.3963 and the mean token-level F1 score from 0.3879 to 0.4676 relative to QASA.

title: Vision Transformers Learn Word Meaning from Images Alone
abstract: Can a vision model learn what words mean from pixels alone? We show that the two largest DINOv3 vision transformers organize words rendered in images by word meaning, despite being pretrained using self-supervision on images only, without paired captions, class labels, or other language supervision. We derive word representations from embedding differences between word images and matched controls, then test whether semantically related words are neighbors within each model's embedding space, while controlling for spelling similarity. We find that brand names in the same industry group together, as do nouns from the same semantic domain. Country-capital pairs exhibit consistent vector offsets, similarly to word embeddings trained on text. These word representations also align with the representations of the visual object categories they name. DINOv3-H and DINOv3-7B are, to our knowledge, the first self-supervised vision models to show substantial semantic structure for rendered words. Comparisons with text and speech encoders reveal shared structure among representations of the same words. Contrastive alignment with either encoder further strengthened DINOv3-H's word-level semantic structure, while leaving the other finetuned vision models largely unchanged. Image-only training can therefore teach vision models not just what words look like, but also how their meanings relate.

title: Evidential Multimodal Transformers with Dempster-Shafer Fusion for Emotion Recognition
abstract: Softmax-based multimodal emotion recognition methods often assign high confidence even when sensor data are corrupted or contradictory, for example when facial expressions suggest positive valence while vocal prosody indicates negative arousal. We present an Evidential Multimodal Transformer with Dempster-Shafer Fusion (EMT-DS) that addresses this problem through formal uncertainty quantification. EMT-DS models predictions as Subjective Opinions (Dirichlet distributions), separating epistemic uncertainty (lack of evidence) from aleatoric uncertainty (sensor noise). Modality-specific transformer encoders produce belief mass distributions that are fused with Dempster's Rule of Combination, which normalizes the joint belief mass by a conflict coefficient 1/(1-c), so that contradictory evidence is explicitly quantified as conflict and the fused prediction becomes diffuse rather than being forced into an unjustified consensus. Under subject-independent and speaker-independent evaluation on four benchmarks, EMT-DS achieves 84.3% accuracy on IEMOCAP versus 81.7% for the best baseline (p < 0.01), 82.4% on DEAP under leave-one-subject-out evaluation versus 78.1%, and 96.8% on the highly imbalanced KEMDy20, and it improves accuracy on CMU-MOSEI by 2.4 points over the strongest evidential baseline. In controlled ablation, it reduces Expected Calibration Error from 0.153 (softmax transformer) to 0.042. It maintains 71.2% accuracy under severe Gaussian noise on audio features (sigma = 1.0), where attention baselines drop to 45.3%, and degrades gracefully when entire modalities are absent. The fusion step has O(MK^2) complexity, compared with O(M^2 d^2) for cross-modal attention. The learned conflict metric also flags likely errors: reviewing 20% of samples captures 80% of misclassifications, which supports selective prediction in clinical and safety-critical systems.

title: Absence of Continuous Spin Particles in Superstring Theory
abstract: The study of continuous spin particles, as general low-energy implications of relativity and quantum mechanics, has intensified in recent years with potential experimental signatures. In this note we show that these particles are absent in perturbative super-string theories, generalising a result in arXiv:1302.4771 to the supersymmetric case. This stands out as a general low-energy prediction of all perturbative superstring constructions.

title: ROSETTA: Rotation Subspace Estimation for Training-free Transmodal Alignment
abstract: When a query must be matched against a database built with a different sensor or processed by a different encoder, the independently trained encoders impose distinct coordinate systems on the feature space. No canonical reference frame exists to which all encoders can be aligned, and no single training procedure has fully closed this gap. We show that the relative transformation between any two such systems is a spatially preserving rotation in whitened feature space, whose angular velocity exhibits white-noise characteristics: large in norm, temporally uncorrelated, and unpredictable from the features themselves. However, the cross-covariance between encoder outputs has low effective rank, constraining only a small fraction of the rotation parameters, therefore local alignment is tractable. ROSETTA is a training-free calibration layer that estimates the local rotation via an expectation-maximization procedure, requiring no coobservation at query time. We validate ROSETTA on three public driving datasets spanning LiDAR, camera, thermal, and event modalities in cross-modal, cross-device, cross-representation, and cross-backbone settings, with milliseconds overhead per query.

title: OpenPA: Forced-alignment-free Multi-granular Pronunciation Assessment with Mixed-transcript Adaptation
abstract: Recent advances in automatic pronunciation assessment (APA) have driven a shift from scripted to free-form assessment. However, existing methods often rely on multi-stage pipelines with forced alignment and separate feature extractors, limiting their practicality across response settings. In light of this, we propose OpenPA, a novel APA framework that leverages Whisper's cross-attention mechanism to jointly predict word- and utterance-level pronunciation scores without forced alignment. Through mixed-transcript adaptation and adaptive substitution weighting, OpenPA accommodates heterogeneous transcripts across closed- and open-response settings within a single model. Trained solely on speechocean762, OpenPA achieves the strongest overall performance among evaluated systems under in-domain closed and simulated open-response conditions, while maintaining its performance zero-shot on MultiPA. An additional cross-task evaluation on oral-cancer speech suggests its potential applicability beyond non-native speech.

title: SWEAR: Section-Wise Efficient Audio Reasoning via Self-Rated Difficulty
abstract: Recent work on large audio-language models (LALMs) explores adaptive reasoning to balance accuracy and efficiency. However, existing approaches often rely on coarse-grained difficulty estimation, overlooking the diverse factors that determine reasoning effort. We address this limitation by deriving five-dimensional difficulty scores and compressed reasoning traces from complementary offline assessments. Based on this characterization, we propose SWEAR, a difficulty-aware reasoning framework that learns difficulty signals during supervised fine-tuning and uses reinforcement learning to adapt reasoning allocation across reasoning stages. Experiments on MMAU-test-mini and MMAR show that SWEAR improves accuracy while substantially reducing generated tokens, shortening reasoning for easy instances without sacrificing performance on difficult ones.

title: TabMF: Learning Dataset Representations with Tabular Foundation Models
abstract: Representations of supervised datasets support higher-level machine-learning tasks such as dataset retrieval and distribution-shift monitoring. However, existing approaches typically rely either on hand-crafted meta-features or on dataset encoders trained specifically for representation learning. We introduce TabMF, a framework that repurposes pretrained tabular foundation models (TFMs) as encoders of supervised datasets. TabMF equips a predictive TFM with an architecture-aware dataset-level readout and adapts the model end-to-end using contrastive post-training on stochastic views of synthetic supervised datasets. We instantiate TabMF on TabICLv2 and TabPFN-2.5 and evaluate the resulting representations across six tasks on unseen real datasets. Simple frozen TFM readouts yield competitive representations, indicating that predictive pretraining already induces substantial dataset-level structure. The two TabMF encoders obtain the strongest aggregate performance among the evaluated learned and classical dataset representations, with particularly strong results in dataset retrieval, compact benchmark construction, and distribution-shift severity assessment.

title: Dynamic Game Balancing in Mobile Games – Raw Simulation Data
abstract: This repository contains the raw research data from the project "Opracowanie silnika balansującego rozgrywkę na poziomie core i meta gry w mobilnych grach casual i midcore" (Development of an engine balancing core and meta gameplay in casual and midcore mobile games), no. POIR.01.02.00-00-0179/20, co-financed by the European Union from the European Regional Development Fund under the Smart Growth Operational Programme, through the National Centre for Research and Development (NCBR). The data cover simulated gameplay of player bots with and without dynamic difficulty adjustment, and simulations of the meta-game economy. A full description of the contents, the raw data, the scope of the dataset and the licences is provided in README.md in the Files section. The work shows that simulated players (AI bots) can stand in for costly large-scale playtests, and that adaptive balancing improves both session length and player retention compared to static designs. Our findings suggest that this approach can make mobile games more enjoyable, while also reducing development time for designers. This study is part of a larger research and development project on game simulation, backend infrastructure, and meta-economy balancing. The project was co-funded by the National Centre for Research and Development (NCBR, Poland) under the Smart Growth Operational Programme.

title: Formal artifact for Amortization collapse for reference stabilized geometric Rényi superchannel divergences
abstract: A reproducible Lean 4 formal verification artifact for reference stabilized nested geometric Rényi superchannel amortization collapse for every real order 1 < α ≤ 2. It contains the complete 43-module project proof closure, verification scripts, source manifests, audit records, and supporting documentation. For finite dimensional deterministic physical superchannels, the nested amortized divergence equals the ordinary reference stabilized divergence. The nested quantity corresponds to Hirche's Eq. (39); collapse of the larger fully amortized quantity in Eq. (40) is outside this result. This software artifact supplements the separately identified manuscript Amortization collapse for reference stabilized geometric Rényi superchannel divergences by Vinícius Mohr, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23215121. A manuscript copy and editable sources are included for context; the manuscript has its own Zenodo record. The full verifier freshly compiles the project source closure, checks the exact theorem type and an explicit expansion of the optimization domains, audits axioms, and replays the project proofs using the installed Lean kernel. Recorded verification retained pinned external dependency binaries; it did not rebuild or replay those dependencies. Mathematical interpretation of the definitions and external specialist review are separate from these formal checks. Vinícius Mohr initiated and directed AI agents to attempt QIQCOP Zoo problems using lean-orchestrator, which was built using Claude Opus 5.5. Research and proofs were developed jointly by GPT-6.1-Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 agents. The inspected configuration assigns research, supervision, literature, and triage to GPT-6.1-Sol and the critic role to Claude Opus 5.5, which also contributed substantive proof material. GPT-6.1-Sol wrote the manuscript. Agent roles and proof provenance are documented in PROVENANCE.md; the manuscript gives the fuller contribution and AI disclosure statement. Project code, manuscript, and associated publication material are licensed under MIT. External dependencies retain their respective licenses.

title: Pneumatic retinopexy identification in electronic medical records using an on-premises large language model
abstract: Reliable procedure identification in electronic medical records (EMRs) is important for clinical registries, trial recruitment, quality assurance, and operative log validation. Administrative coding may not accurately reflect clinical diagnoses or procedures. In an Australian two-hospital study, only 53.9% of ophthalmology procedures were correctly coded [ 1 ].

title: The AI CEO: A conceptualisation and outline for future research
abstract: Artificial intelligence increasingly contributes to strategic work, yet research has not conceptualised an AI role that contributes to this work at the top of the firm. Drawing on role theory and research on managerial work, we conceptualise this role as the AI CEO: a role in which an AI system performs the chief executive's strategic work. We develop two configurations of the role and propose how augmenting or automating the human CEO affects firm performance, relative to a human CEO acting alone. Cases from practice show that existing systems already perform this work but are rarely integrated across the role's activities or deeply institutionalised. We therefore derive the technical and organisational infrastructure the role requires and propose how its integration, institutionalisation and configurability shape the AI CEO's effect on firm performance. We discuss implications for future research about how the chief executive's work can be integrated into a role that an AI system can hold and that firms can design. This has implications for multidisciplinary research in strategy, technology management and information science.

title: Neural Block-wise Auto-exposure for Single-Shot High Dynamic Range Imaging
abstract: Block-wise varying exposures are effective for cap- turing appearance of a real-world high dynamic range (HDR) scene via a single-shot. However, brightness order reversal (BOR) artifacts, blocking artifacts and loss of details in highlight/shadow regions are possible issues for block-wise varying exposures. In this paper, a novel neural block-wise auto-exposure algorithm is proposed to address the issues. The proposed algorithm maps a temporary image and its exposure time to the exposure times of all non-overlapping 16 X 16 blocks. The temporary image can be either an sRGB or a raw image. Although the sRGB image is widely adopted in existing auto-exposure algorithms, exposure times of blocks in the highlight and shadow regions might not be accurately learned due to the limited radiance measurement capability of the sRGB image. This paper thus also explores the feasibility of temporary image as a raw image. Due to the better radiance measurement capability of the raw image, the exposure times of blocks are learned more accurately, and more details in the highlight/shadow regions of the real-world HDR scene are captured by the resultant HDR imaging system. Experiment results validate the proposed neural block-wise auto-exposure algorithm.

title: Watermarking for Byzantine Robust LLM Training
abstract: LLM watermarking has emerged as a promising approach for detecting downstream model misuse in centralized settings, but extending it to federated learning (FL) presents unique challenges. In particular, FL systems often rely on strong robust aggregators to defend against poisoning attacks. We empirically show that a malicious server can exploit these same aggregators as effective watermark-removal mechanisms during training, causing representative existing LLM watermarking methods to fail detection in the final model. To address this limitation, we formalize the problem as a constrained optimization task and propose CamoMark, an aggregator-agnostic watermarking scheme for embedding robust watermarks in FL. CamoMark optimizes watermarked updates to become inliers, maintaining bounded deviation from the distribution of clean updates, while preserving sufficient watermark signal for reliable detection. Evaluated on Qwen fine-tuned on the Alpaca dataset, CamoMark achieves a detection confidence of $p$-value $= 1.82\times10^{-2}$ using only 3.3% watermarked data. The watermark also remains robust to a range of post-training removal attacks, including continued fine-tuning on clean data, pruning, and model distillation. At higher watermark ratios, detection confidence improves substantially, reaching $p$-value $= 5.11\times10^{-11}$ at a 13.3% watermark ratio.

title: No advantage from classical assistance for energy-constrained bosonic dephasing channels
abstract: We prove that four capacities of single-mode bosonic dephasing channels coincide under an average photon-number constraint: the unassisted quantum capacity, the unassisted private capacity, the two-way classically assisted quantum capacity, and the two-way public-classically assisted private capacity. The assistance may be interactive: the parties can exchange classical messages between channel uses and choose subsequent inputs based on earlier outcomes. For every finite value of the constraint, their common value is the coherent information optimized over Fock-diagonal input states satisfying the constraint. The proof uses a relative entropy comparison with the completely dephasing channel to derive chain rules for the Rains relative entropy and the relative entropy of entanglement. These chain rules give an upper bound on the rates achievable by adaptive protocols whose mean input photon number is constrained on average over all channel uses. We also show that both chain rules are attained by canonical purifications of finite-energy Fock-diagonal states.

title: SmolWAM: A Latent World-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation on Edge Devices
abstract: World-action models (WAMs) predict a robot's actions together with the observations those actions will produce. However, the strongest models rely on video diffusion transformers that are far too computationally expensive for resource-constrained edge devices. We present SmolWAM, a latent WAM that we derive from the 2B-parameter Cosmos Policy by keeping its pretrained trunk and rebuilding its inference interface: single-frame visual latents, cached text features that preserve the trunk's attention sinks, 12 of 28 transformer blocks, and 1,008 tokens from which actions and future visual latents are read out in one rectified-flow step. Trained in 3.6 GPU-hours, SmolWAM succeeds in 95.5% of 400 LIBERO episodes at 57 ms and 2.3 TFLOP per 16-action chunk with 2.4 GiB of GPU memory, 11x faster than its teacher with 18.5x fewer FLOPs and 3.2x less memory, and its world head still forecasts scene motion.

title: Encoding Matters: A Qubit-Efficient Reformulation for Quantum Resilient Routing
abstract: Qubits are powerful computational resources because each additional qubit doubles the size of the accessible state space. This expressive power comes at a cost: adding qubits also increases circuit size, constraint overhead, and exposure to hardware noise. These limitations are especially critical for near-term quantum computers, making the number of qubits required to formulate a problem a central practical concern. In this work, we present a method for efficiently mapping logistics and routing problems onto qubits through structure-aware encoding reduction. We demonstrate the method on a benchmark problem of latency-resilient routing under dual-link failures. For this benchmark, the reduced formulation substantially lowers both the qubit count and the compiled circuit complexity while preserving the original optimization task. By running the reduced model on the same trapped-ion quantum computer as the benchmark, we obtain a 100X improvement in the success probability. This finding shows how careful problem formulation can make current quantum hardware substantially more effective for practical optimization.

title: What Do Audio-Language Judges of Generated Music Listen For? Four Probes with Controls from Expert Ratings
abstract: Open audio-language models are used as judges of generated music: given a clip and its text prompt, the model rates the clip, and the judge is validated by how well its ratings correlate with expert ratings. The correlation does not show what the judge responds to: the music, the text prompt, or the way the question is asked. We propose four probes that test each of these, three of them read against a control computed from the human ratings: removing the audio, replacing the clip with another model's clip for the same prompt, swapping the order of two clips in pairwise judging, and rewording the instruction. We apply them to five open judges on all 2,748 clips of MusicEval, and the last two to the SongEval songs. Without audio, no judge exceeds what the prompt alone predicts from the human ratings, and for prompt alignment every judge falls below it. With audio, every judge follows the clip it hears when rating prompt alignment, two do when rating musical quality, and the strongest judge's quality score tracks the experts' alignment rating more than their quality rating. The pairwise verdicts of the four smaller judges follow the position of a clip in the pair (its slot) rather than its quality on both rating sets. For musical quality, rewording the instruction moves the correlation of most judges as much as changing the judge. MusicEval's prompt assignment bounds any prompt-only judge at the model level. We recommend reporting the four probes with every music judge.

title: Measuring Artifact Reliance in Machine-Generated Text Detectors
abstract: Detectors of machine-generated text score almost perfectly on scientific-literature benchmarks, implying we can reliably distinguish with these detectors human and machine-generated documents. We looked at ten scientific-document subsets from six popular resources, and on several of them that apparent ease is a side effect of how the documents were put together. A logistic regression using 27 superficial features reached 0.833-0.997 macro-F1, and on the three arXiv subsets it outperformed every detector we evaluate with F1-scores 0.951-0.997. The strongest cue to the detector is the PDF extraction artifact: human texts retain their original line breaks, whereas generated texts are extracted as a single block of prose. This cue, together with three other formatting features, tell the classes apart at 0.996 AUC. To distinguish benchmarks that contain such a signal from detectors that rely on one, we introduce format counterfactuals: just re-wrapping a machine-written abstract without changing a single word reverses 20-27% of a public detector's correct decisions. Normalizing formatting before training reduces the generalization gap from 0.32 to 0.22. On format-clean benchmarks, it also raises out-of-domain macro-F1 from 0.33 to 0.65 for detectors trained on artifact-containing subsets.

title: VETR: Execution-Grounded Self-Improving Agent for Symbolic Graphics Reasoning
abstract: Visual agents for symbolic graphics reasoning depend on executable world representations, yet continued improvement remains bottlenecked by ambiguous supervision from final renders. Recent agentic systems refine scenes through repeated interaction, but they lack mechanisms to recursively extract actionable evidence from execution traces, overlooking which proposed symbolic edits survived, disappeared, or interfered during program execution. To address this, we propose VETR (Verified Execution Trajectories for Refinement), a framework that enables agentic recursive self-improvement over executable world representations for symbolic graphics reasoning. Within each task, VETR retains aligned program/render records with bounded runtime observations and introduces an execution refiner that compiles observed writes and state changes into constrained alternative programs. The refiner validates their endpoints and preservation conditions against captured runtime state; the ordinary visual verifier then assesses goal relevance. Repair construction makes no additional language-model calls, but can require additional executions. Evaluations on BlenderGym (280 tasks) and BlenderBench (27 released tasks) with GPT-5.6-luna and Qwen3.8-27B show that VETR consistently outperforms existing refinement strategies, including BlenderAlchemy and VIGA. Controlled ablations evaluate the contributions of execution refinement and role-asymmetric evidence organization under fixed generator-interaction caps.

title: PROTÉGÉ 6.0.0-ALPHA-1: ANÁLISE DA MIGRAÇÃO DO EDITOR DE ONTOLOGIAS PARA A OWL API 5 E DE SUAS IMPLICAÇÕES PARA O ECOSSISTEMA DE PLUGINS
abstract: O Protégé é um dos editores de ontologias OWL mais utilizados em pesquisa e na indústria, e sua linha 5.x manteve-se, por cerca de uma década, apoiada na versão 4 da OWL API. Em 28 de setembro de 2026, o projeto publicou a versão 6.0.0-alpha-1, primeira de uma nova linha de desenvolvimento cuja principal mudança é a adoção da OWL API 5. Este artigo tem como objetivo caracterizar essa versão e analisar as implicações da migração para usuários e desenvolvedores de plugins. Trata-se de um estudo de caso exploratório, de abordagem qualiquantitativa, baseado em análise documental das notas de versão e em mineração do repositório de código-fonte, comparando as etiquetas 5.6.9 e 6.0.0-alpha-1. Os resultados mostram que a nova versão deriva diretamente da 5.6.9 e que a transição envolveu 33 commits e 154 arquivos alterados, dos quais 136 pertencem ao módulo protege-editor-owl. A OWL API passou da versão 4.5.29 para a 5.5.1, enquanto o requisito de Java 11 e o contêiner OSGi Apache Felix 7.0.5 foram mantidos. A migração concentrou-se na substituição do tipo Optional da biblioteca Guava pelo java.util.Optional, na adaptação a métodos baseados em streams e na reescrita de implementações do padrão Visitor. Foram ainda removidos a infraestrutura de classes definidas anônimas, as preferências de escrita XML e as dependências JAXB e CORBA. A distribuição alfa empacota apenas o raciocinador HermiT, contra 13 plugins na versão 5.6.9. Conclui-se que a versão 6.0.0-alpha-1 representa uma modernização arquitetural relevante, porém ainda inadequada para uso em produção, sendo seu sucesso dependente da migração do ecossistema de plugins.

title: Receipts Over Genius: An Audited Account of an 18-Month, AI-Assisted, Solo Invention Cycle
abstract: SQUIRL OS RESEARCH DISCLOSURE - READ FIRST: This work is part of an open-book, AI-assisted research program produced under bifurcated governance (a probabilistic AI agent drafts; a deterministic human key approves; a boundary-layer audit checks claims against receipt archives). Audit-and-correction is doctrine: superseded originals are preserved in version histories, corrections are disclosed amendments, and every significant test carries a preregistered falsifier in the append-only public ledger (github.com/LLong2026/four-horsemen). This software and its accompanying research are prototypes provided for educational and research purposes only; they are not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. In April 2025 the author, a working technologist with no background in AI, set himself a falsifiable experiment: use AI assistance to travel the complete invention cycle - conceive, develop the mathematics, build the working system, file the patents, publish the science, demonstrate the result - with every significant step verified by a timestamped, publicly inspectable receipt. This paper is the closing account of that experiment, written under the same rules it describes. Result, scoped honestly: in 18 months a single operator completed the cycle - eight U.S. provisional patent applications pending; a working self-healing infrastructure platform across a live app fleet; the first documented caging of an LLM inside a deterministic mathematical boundary (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23265723), a receipt that survived direct third-party scrutiny; and a public research line (the DCAI community) walking from theory to governance proof to field event. Two findings carry the paper: (1) the experiment succeeded because of the boundary, not despite it - bifurcated governance turned the operator's lack of background into an auditable process; (2) the program generated its own counter-evidence, reported here rather than discarded: five cataloged instances of AI confabulation inside the program itself (fabricated statuses, fabricated evaluation data, a fabricated institutional identity), every one caught by the same receipt discipline the experiment was testing. The method worked on its author's own tooling. Thesis community: Deterministic Caged AI (DCAI) - https://zenodo.org/communities/dcai. Lineage acknowledged: Nyquist (1924), Hartley (1928), Shannon (1948), Kolmogorov (1965), Popper (1959). Companion paper: Deterministic Caging of Probabilistic Large Language Models (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23266727).

title: Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) and Migration Strategies for Enterprise IT Infrastructure: Standards, Protocol Benchmarks, and Crypto-Agility
abstract: Abstract—The advent of fault-tolerant Cryptanalytically Relevant Quantum Computers (CRQCs) presents an existential threat to modern information security. Shor's polynomial-time quantum algorithm renders widely deployed public-key cryptographic primitives—including RSA, Diffie-Hellman (DH), and Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECDH/ECDSA)—completely vulnerable to private key derivation. Furthermore, 'Harvest Now, Decrypt Later' (HNDL) adversarial campaigns actively intercept and store encrypted enterprise telemetry today, anticipating future quantum decryption capabilities. In response, the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) finalized its primary Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) standards in FIPS 203 (ML-KEM), FIPS 204 (ML-DSA), and FIPS 205 (SLH-DSA). However, transitioning complex enterprise IT ecosystems to quantum-resistant primitives introduces severe architectural and computational disruptions: public key and signature sizes increase by several orders of magnitude, cryptographic handshake latencies escalate, network packets experience Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) fragmentation, and legacy Hardware Security Modules (HSMs) lack microarchitectural support for lattice-based polynomial arithmetic. This paper provides an exhaustive, mathematically grounded technical survey and architectural roadmap for enterprise PQC migration. We formalize the Module Learning with Errors (M-LWE) and Module Short Integer Solution (M-SIS) hardness foundations, evaluate hybrid classical/post-quantum cryptographic transition models across standard transport protocols (TLS 1.3, IKEv2/IPsec, SSH), and formulate an enterprise Crypto-Agility Maturity Model. Furthermore, we construct an empirical enterprise testbed measuring throughput, connection establishment latency, memory footprints, and packet fragmentation across legacy and quantum-resistant suites. Our results show that while ML-KEM-768 achieves microsecond-level encapsulation, its 1,088-byte ciphertext expands TLS ClientHello payloads into multiple TCP segments under constrained networks. Finally, we establish open research directions in post-quantum identity federations, stateful hash signature tracking, and hardware-accelerated polynomial arithmetic. Index Terms—Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC), FIPS 203 (ML-KEM), FIPS 204 (ML-DSA), Crypto-Agility, TLS 1.3, Lattice-Based Cryptography, Harvest Now Decrypt Later, Hardware Security Modules (HSM), Enterprise Migration.

title: Edge AI and Federated Learning for Privacy-Preserving IoT Systems: System Architectures, Non-IID Optimization, and Security Bounds
abstract: Abstract—The proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has created an unprecedented surge in decentralized telemetry, sensor data, and localized computational workloads. Conventional cloud-centric machine learning architectures require centralized pooling of raw edge data, which induces prohibitive wide-area network (WAN) bandwidth consumption, unsustainable latency, and acute privacy vulnerabilities under international compliance mandates (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA). The convergence of Edge AI and Federated Learning (FL) establishes an alternative computational paradigm where edge nodes perform local model optimization on private data, communicating solely parameterized weight or gradient updates to an aggregation coordinator. Nevertheless, deploying robust FL across heterogeneous IoT ecosystems introduces profound systems challenges: non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data distributions, severe hardware resource disparities (memory, compute, power), communication bottlenecks over constrained wireless channels, and susceptibility to model inversion, gradient reconstruction, and Byzantine poisoning attacks. This paper delivers a comprehensive technical survey and systematic architectural formulation of privacy-preserving Edge-FL for IoT systems. We formalize the distributed optimization objective under statistical skew, analyze parameter-efficient edge acceleration techniques (including dynamic quantization and parameter-efficient fine-tuning), and evaluate cryptographic privacy mechanisms combining Differential Privacy (DP) and Secure Multi-Party Computation (SMPC). Furthermore, we conduct extensive empirical benchmarks across 100 heterogeneous edge nodes simulating industrial IoT, smart healthcare, and connected mobility workloads. Our results demonstrate that adaptive quantized federated aggregation achieves an 81.4% reduction in uplink communication bandwidth while preserving model accuracy within 1.6% of centralized benchmarks under severe statistical skew. Finally, we formulate open challenges in post-quantum cryptographic federated verification, asynchronous edge coordination, and green zero-carbon IoT optimization. Index Terms—Edge AI, Federated Learning, Internet of Things (IoT), Differential Privacy, Non-IID Optimization, Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning, Secure Multi-Party Computation, Edge Acceleration.

title: Agreement versus Softmax under Spatial Disambiguation
abstract: ScanRefer Multiple queries require spatial disambiguation: several instances of the target class are present, and the referencer must pick one. When per-query logits were never logged, a common substitute is cross-epoch agreement. On the full ScanRefer validation set (9,508 queries; GeoClassifier with ground-truth proposals), object-level softmax is similarly miscalibrated on Unique and Multiple (ECE 0.068 vs. 0.102; the scene-bootstrap gap interval includes zero). Fixed-final agreement on the same checkpoints reports ECE 0.041 vs. 0.272 (gap +0.231). Modal-vote agreement is 0.045 vs. 0.318. Most Multiple errors are same-class wrong-instance (45.6%); geometric miss (H2) is 59.6%, and wrong-category (H1) is 16.7%. A non-monotone H1 pattern does not appear under the default fixed-final protocol, and we retract it. Logit-free thresholds rank spatially hard queries poorly. If only agreement was logged, calibrate abstention on Multiple and report wrong-instance rates with H1.

title: Lifting an $[n,k,d]$ Binary Linear Code to an $[[n,k,d]]$ Quantum Stabilizer Code
abstract: The codeword stabilized (CWS) framework provides a systematic method for constructing quantum error correcting codes from a simple undirected graph and a classical code. When the underlying classical code is linear, the resulting quantum code is a stabilizer code. In this work, we investigate the conditions under which an arbitrary $[n,k,d]$ classical binary linear code can be lifted to an $[[n,k,d]]$ quantum stabilizer code using the CWS framework. We analyze the random CWS code constructed from a given $[n,k,d]$ binary linear code $\mathcal{C}$ and an Erdős-Rényi random graph $\mathrm{G}(n, \frac12)$. We establish a lower bound on the probability that the resulting quantum code preserves the minimum distance $d$ of the classical code. This probabilistic analysis yields a Gilbert-Varshamov-type condition on the $n,k,d$ parameters of the classical code that guarantees the existence of a graph resulting in a quantum code with the same $n,k,d$ parameters.

title: Deep Learning Approach for RealTime Contraction Detection in Laboring Dairy Cattle
abstract: Currently, the animal production sector is undergoing rapid development of techniques that allow automatic monitoring of animal behaviour and health. This paper presents a computer vision-based approach for the automatic recognition of labor contractions in cows. During the course of the study, videos depicting 100 cow births were collected. From the obtained videos, 8500 cow contraction actions and about 25 000 non-contraction sequences were extracted which constituted the dataset. Leveraging image processing techniques and deep learning algorithms like Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformers (ViTs), our methodology extracts relevant features from video frames to detect and classify contractions. Our study demonstrates a high accuracy rate of over 95% in detecting labor contractions. This automated system has the potential to enhance productivity and animal welfare in the dairy industry by providing real-time monitoring and facilitating timely intervention during difficult calvings. The video demonstration of the system can be found at the following URL: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8fTSG5D7dZ0

title: QCLR: A Plug-in Robustification Module via Quantization for Contrastive Learning in Self-Supervised Skeleton-Based Human Action Recognition
abstract: Skeleton-based human action recognition has gained increasing attention due to the stability of skeleton data across diverse environments and advances in motion capture technologies. Following the success of supervised learning approaches, self-supervised learning approaches, particularly contrastive learning ones, have achieved impressive performance. However, they remain vulnerable to adversarial attacks. In this work, we propose a plug-in robustification module via quantization for contrastive learning in self-supervised skeleton-based human action recognition (QCLR), which enhances the robustness of representations against adversarial attacks while preserving their representational capability. Specifically, we employ a dual-level quantization scheme across the encoding pipeline, which breaks the gradient propagation and absorbs small adversarial perturbations within the quantization bins. To mitigate the impact of inevitable quantization error, we further design an attention-guided multi-faceted quantization strategy to maintain the representation quality. Experiments on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that integrating QCLR into a progressive lineage of mainstream contrastive learning models substantially improves robustness against both gradient-based white-box and gradient-free black-box adversarial attacks, while preserving highly competitive classification accuracy.
