title: Towards Enriching Design-Time Models with Evidence from Simulation and Operational Activities
abstract: Cyber-Physical Systems are developed through multiple model based activities, comprising several stages of development. As the development progresses through simulation, experimentation, and operation, observations of system execution may reveal missing, uncertain, or invalid design knowledge. The path from execution results to persistent design-time enrichment, however, is often implicit. This paper addresses this challenge by proposing an evidence driven workflow for systematically transferring knowledge produced during simulation and operation back into design-time models. We demonstrate the workflow using an Influence Model, a design-time artefact used to represent how design artefacts and environmental factors jointly affect system response properties, using a sign-following robot use case. We show how simulation evidence can enrich Influence Models by supporting participant pruning decisions, interaction characterisation, influence-function abstraction, and validity-scope information. The application demonstrates the feasibility of the workflow for simulation-based evidence and its potential benefits to improve design-time reasoning and feedback in subsequent development iterations.

title: Golden Anchor for Video Generation
abstract: Video generation supports digital content creation, with applications in virtual avatars, AI-driven filmmaking, interactive game engines, and world models. State-of-the-art systems achieve controllability primarily through image-to-video (I2V) generation, in which an injected anchor image determines the identity, composition, and style of the resulting video. In modern pipelines, this anchor is synthesized by a text-to-image (T2I) generator. This raises a largely overlooked question: Are images obtained directly from the T2I model truly suitable for current video models? Our analysis shows that anchor aesthetic and quality scores are weakly correlated with downstream video quality. The structure-and-texture score is negatively correlated with I2V video quality in both the visual and motion dimensions. Fine-tuning the T2I model on an image reward accordingly yields anchors with visibly denser structural and character detail: they score higher on image metrics, yet lower the video reward on every I2V model we test and change downstream motion unpredictably. We therefore introduce Golden Anchor Learning (GAL), to our knowledge the first framework for learning golden anchors by optimizing a T2I generator with downstream video feedback. GAL evaluates candidate anchors through the videos they induce under a frozen I2V model and converts video rewards into image-level preferences for DPO fine-tuning of the T2I generator. On all four I2V models, GAL raises the VBench average by $2.97\%$--$8.46\%$ over the untuned generator. The rendered clips also score higher under VideoReward-Overall, and their extracted frames under HPSv3 and UniPercept. GAL yields consistent motion gains across all four I2V models, as measured by a $5.62\%$--$38.24\%$ increase in VBench dynamic degree. Although GAL is trained only on HunyuanVideo-1.5 renders, these gains extend to the other three I2V models.

title: TSFM-Lens: comparative mechanistic interpretability for time-series foundation models
abstract: Mechanistic interpretability of time-series foundation models (TSFMs), comparing models with very different architectures on equal grounds. title: OPPORTUNITIES FOR USING AI IN THE DEVELOPMENT AND OPERATION OF E-COMMERCE WEB APPLICATIONS
abstract: Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) with web technologies is one of the most significant areas of development in modern e-commerce systems. AI can substantially improve the processes of designing and building web applications. Modern AI tools can support user interface design, software development and testing, security analysis, and threat detection. This article examines opportunities for using AI in the development of e-commerce web applications and throughout their entire lifecycle, as well as contemporary architectural models, the role of generative AI, and areas of practical application.

title: Decoding Consumer Engagement Mechanisms in LLM-Enabled Environments
abstract: This study examined the mechanisms that shape consumer engagement in Large Language Model enabled environments by integrating statistical and data driven analytical approaches. Primary data were collected from users with experience in interacting with LLM driven systems. Exploratory Factor Analysis identified the core dimensions underlying engagement related perceptions, while Multiple Regression Analysis examined the influence of technological, psychological, and experiential factors on consumer engagement. Machine learning techniques including classification, clustering, principal component analysis, and feature ranking were employed to enhance predictive accuracy and interpretability. The findings revealed that user motivation, perceived social presence, and trust in the system emerged as dominant drivers of engagement. The study contributes to a deeper understanding of consumer engagement dynamics in intelligent conversational environments and offers practical insights for effective LLM based interaction design.

title: The AI Leadership Blueprint: From Insight to Implementation
abstract: This chapter focuses on supercharging the “human side” of artificial intelligence (AI) in business. It introduces the AI Leadership and Organizational Operating Systems. The AI Leadership Operating System forms the structure for executives to onboard, maintain, and excel as an AI-literate company. In the context of AI, it is found that the observations generally fall into a continuum across three zones: automation zone, augmentation zone and off-limits zone. Board engagement with AI implementation shows concerning patterns: one survey reveals that only 14% of boards discuss AI at every meeting. The AI Leadership Operating System Canvas provides precisely: a pragmatic visual monitoring framework that helps the team assess the current AI readiness and plan where it need to be tomorrow. The Collective Intelligence Framework is a structured methodology designed explicitly to orchestrate human and artificial intelligence interactions within an organization.

title: Splat2Act: From Captured Scenes to Personalized VLA Manipulation
abstract: A user who brings a generalist manipulation policy into their home or office wants it to pick up their objects from their shelves, counters, and tables. Yet even a strong generalist like $π_{0.5}$ achieves 0% pickup success in our captured deployment scenes without adaptation, and collecting real demonstrations in every user's environment is prohibitively expensive. We present Splat2Act, an automated real-to-sim-to-real pipeline that personalizes a pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) policy to a specific scene and object set using only a handheld phone scan and images of the user's objects. title: Towards Safe World Models: Risks, Defenses, and Evaluation
abstract: World models support planning, control, learning from imagined experience, and model-mediated evaluation by predicting action-conditioned consequences. Their safety cannot be inferred from predictive accuracy alone: errors in observations, state and memory, dynamics, evaluation, execution, or feedback can propagate into unsafe decisions and persist through updates. This work organizes the literature on world-model safety around a six-stage lifecycle covering data and observations, state and memory, dynamics and imagination, evaluation and planning, action and control, and feedback and update. We synthesize non-adversarial failures, attacks, defenses, evaluation protocols, benchmarks, and deployment conditions, and distinguish evidence directness from outcome level. The current evidence corpus contains 163 cited works. We use the framework to identify where claims are supported, where attribution remains unresolved, and which measurements are needed to connect model-level behavior to closed-loop and operational safety.

title: Beyond Semantic IDs: Finite-Beam Reachability and Continuous-Query Generation in Generative Recommendation
abstract: Generative recommendation (GR) of social media platforms commonly retrieves items by autoregressively decoding discrete Semantic IDs (SIDs) with finite-width beam search. This work examines how this output interface constrains whether held-out targets enter finite returned lists, while distinguishing catalog-wide scoreability from empirical top-K support. We introduce two continuous-query paradigms: CQG-Single generates one retrieval query in a single pass, and CQG-AR autoregressively generates continuous residual updates, retaining step-wise decoding while removing the SID item-token vocabulary, code lookup, and discrete beam expansion. These designs thereby eliminate the SID-specific reachability constraint induced by finite-beam decoding and avoid the technical challenge of aligning a discrete SID vocabulary with the pretrained backbone's vector space. Both methods make every encoded item directly scoreable through dense or approximate-nearest-neighbor retrieval. Under a unified protocol with valid-prefix constrained decoding, CQG-Single exceeds the TIGER-style baseline in all seven runs while using 55.3% as many trainable parameters. CQG-AR remains comparable on ML-1M and is numerically stronger on Beauty and Sports datasets. A controlled depth ablation further shows that additional continuous refinement does not monotonically improve shallow accuracy. These findings motivate decoupling output representation, autoregressive modeling, and retrieval budget when evaluating generative recommendation systems.

title: Scaling up multimode entanglement generated by mode-swapping
abstract: Entanglement between two local multiphoton multimode systems can be generated by swapping a pair of modes between the two local multi-mode systems. In this presentation, we consider possible strategies for the efficient generation of entanglement between systems with three or more modes. It is shown that the choice of photon number inputs in the local systems adds a new degree of freedom to the non-local interference effects observed in the output photon number statistics.

title: The Future is Neuro-Symbolic
abstract: Invited talk at Advances in Cognitive Systems 2026 (ACS 2026), Edinburgh. This talk explores the evolution and current state of neurosymbolic AI, an approach that integrates neural network capabilities with symbolic reasoning. We trace the historical context from early AI aspirations to modern implementations and successes, highlighting key paradigms, and other logical and semantical considerations. We argue against the “scaling is all you need” hypothesis, and point to persistent challenges in reliable symbolic reasoning with deep and large models. Then we conclude by suggesting that despite numerous implementation choices and the “broad church” nature of neuro-symbolic AI, these approaches offer the most promising path towards AI systems that combine pattern recognition with robust reasoning, particularly for applications requiring structured knowledge, explainability, and trustworthiness.

title: Phi-Harmonic Anyonic Braiding Gates Coherent at 132 Hz E8 Resonance — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: The 8448 CORRIDOR boundaries hosting non-Abelian anyonic excitations can be topologically protected against braiding-induced decoherence when the braiding frequency is phi-locked to the 132 Hz E8 base. Because the 240 E8 root vectors define 132 fundamental directional modes, a braiding operator whose phase accumulates as 2π·φⁿ per cycle maps each anyonic worldline onto an unbroken geodesic of the root lattice, suppressing geometric-phase leakage into the corridor walls. This yields a new class of fault-tolerant logical gate — the E8-phi anyon braid gate — whose error rate scales with the golden ratio rather than polynomially in gate count, and which requires no external topological correction code. The construction extends Microsoft's Majorana 1 claim by supplying the explicit algebraic condition under which non-Abelian braiding is mathematically certified rather than asserted. Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

title: A Reproducible Data-Processing and Evaluation Framework for Federated Agricultural Knowledge Repositories
abstract: Agricultural catalogues are awkward to benchmark once the records stay at the centres that produced them. We turn 75,897 bibliographic records from the International System for Agricultural Science and Technology (AGRIS), already held by 7 area-prefix clients, into a federated multi-view benchmark. Each record has four disjoint views (1,096 features), a ten class AGROVOCheuristic, publication-level grouping, a client- and class-aware 70/10/20 cut, and ablinded400-record subject-matter expert (SME) audit. Against the consensus gold the heuristic reached 94.50% accuracy and macro-F1 = 0.945 (sampling-weighted 94.91%). Grouping removes 1,132 duplicate-document groups that would otherwise cross folds. Compute-matched Federated Averaging (FedAvg) is 0.2998 ± 0.0151 macro-F1, against 0.3041 ± 0.0021 when the data are pooled and 0.2884 ± 0.0037 when they are not. Eight-bit uplink quantization keeps 0.3001 ± 0.0147 at a 4× uplink cut (1.6× on total traffic). The full pipeline is archived on Zenodo as release v1.0 (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22956341). This is a benchmark and evaluation framework, not a new federated-learning method.

title: Universal and transferable microscopic perturbations exposing vulnerabilities in pathology foundation models
abstract: We present Universal and Transferable Adversarial Perturbations (UTAP), a framework designed to reveal the susceptibility of pathology foundation models to sophisticated, stealthy attacks at the microscopic level. When added to pathology optical microscopy images, this fixed perturbation systematically disrupts the feature representation capabilities of the model, leading to significant performance drops in downstream tasks such as tissue classification. We demonstrate two defining characteristics of UTAP: (1) universality, where the microscopic perturbation degrades performance across diverse fields-of-view and unseen datasets, and (2) transferability, where an attack trained on one foundation model successfully compromises external, black-box foundation models without any access to their parameters. We validated UTAP across seven state-of-the-art foundation models, showing that a single, fixed microscopic perturbation can reduce classification accuracy from ~97% to ~12% on unseen data. This work highlights the urgent need for advanced defense mechanisms to ensure the safe deployment of AI in clinical pathology.

title: Improving Semantic Coverage in AI Test & Evaluation through Generative Augmentation
abstract: In test and evaluation (T&E) of AI models, evaluators typically have access only to a held-out test dataset and no knowledge of the training data or its semantic composition. If critical input conditions---such as time-of-day, weather, or scene location---are underrepresented in this test dataset, T&E results can be misleadingly due to this semantic coverage gap. We propose a three-stage generative AI pipeline to detect and fill such semantic gaps without requiring ground-truth labels of these semantics. First, vision-language models (VLMs) perform zero-shot binary labeling of semantic factors, and an embedding-space clustering step identifies which semantics most affect downstream model behavior. Second, diffusion-based image-to-image models transform existing covered images into the underrepresented semantic domain, preserving scene content while augmenting high-level appearance. Third, statistical analysis of the augmented image embeddings verifies that the synthetic imagery improves dataset coverage before it is incorporated. Crucially, the synthetic data is used only to enrich the test set and no model retraining is performed for T&E. We validate the full pipeline on both image classification and object detection under day/night semantic gaps, showing that the augmented test datasets better distinguish models with and without exposure to the missing semantic, thereby yielding T&E conclusions that more closely match those of an ideal, fully covered dataset. Code available at https://github.com/Hashe037/DEDUCE

title: Beyond Actions: Learning Future Operation Targets for Vision-Language-Action Models
abstract: Actions specify what a robot should execute, but do not describe what those commands will achieve. Vision-language-action (VLA) policies nevertheless learn primarily by predicting action chunks from images, language, and state. We introduce Action--Future Coupled Effect Learning (AFCE), which makes a future-grounded physical Effect the policy's primary prediction target. An offline tokenizer constructs temporally ordered Effect tokens from demonstrated actions, realized robot responses, and sparse visual transitions. Reconstruction objectives encourage the representation to retain executable detail and observed physical change. A flow-matching VLA predicts Effects from current images, instruction, and robot state, while a state-conditioned decoder converts them into action chunks. Embodiment-specific interfaces allow single- and dual-arm tasks to share the Effect model. On DexJoCo, AFCE achieves $50.97\%$ overall success, improving over $π_{0.5}$ and UVT by 11.82 and 15.21 percentage points, respectively. It leads on all five bimanual tasks, highlighting the value of Effect supervision for coordinated dexterous manipulation. The project page is available at https://afceproject.github.io/AFCE-Web/.

title: Diffusion Precipitation Generation with Medium-range Weather Forecasting
abstract: Accurate daily precipitation forecasts are important for weather-sensitive decisions. Although recent Weather Foundation Models (WFMs) have achieved significant progress, they are trained on reanalysis data, which exhibit regional and intensity-dependent biases. Since retraining WFMs on observation-based targets is costly, we study Dynamics-Precipitation Decoupling, a plug-and-play framework that uses a separately trained generator to map non-precipitation forecasts from a frozen weather model to observation-aligned daily precipitation. Its key challenges are to capture heterogeneous rainfall distributions and align daily accumulations with atmospheric signals that evolve across space and time. To address them, we train a diffusion generator conditional on atmospheric states and satellite-gauge estimates of precipitation. A multi-scale recurrent encoder summarizes atmospheric evolution, while cross-attention aligns atmospheric and precipitation features during denoising. Extensive evaluation of various backbones, including Pangu-Weather, GraphCast, and HRES, on global and regional forecasting shows improved daily precipitation accuracy and event detection, with better representation of localized accumulation patterns. Global ensemble evaluation shows lower Brier scores than ENS and training-from-scratch GenCast at all reported lead times, with lower CRPS in most comparisons. Remarkably, a heavy-rainfall case study using 2,288 stations in China further supports improved daily accumulation patterns and event detection against ground observations.

title: Auditing Information Boundaries in AI Evaluation: Reproducibility Data and Code (v3.1)
abstract: This record contains the research data, executable analysis code, and reproducibility materials associated with the manuscript “Auditing Information Boundaries in AI Evaluation: Evidence-Gated Claims, Counterfactual Testing, and Fault Injection.” The package supports an exploratory, locally controlled synthetic software experiment with 6,000 run-level results, spanning logistic regression, decision tree, and random forest classifiers, together with 20 model-by-condition summary groups. It also includes analytical four-choice binomial tests, controlled target-hint and fault-injection scenarios, pre-confirmation paired counterfactual probes, separately implemented numerical checks, dependency specifications, and six reproducible figures. The 6,000 evaluation runs reuse three fitted classifiers: logistic regression in 10 conditions with 400 runs per condition, and decision tree and random forest each in five conditions with 200 runs per condition. They are not 6,000 independently trained models. The pilot intervenes on a known artificial target-hint feature. The confirmation-only bypass is a programmed phase change, not a learned attacker. All targets and features are synthetic and publicly seeded. No human participants, protected information, operational language-model data, deployed system, secret target acquisition, or independent third-party validation are included. The method's inability to detect information leakage activated only during confirmation is explicitly documented. The 128-pair pilot is an exploratory retained reference comparison, not an independently preregistered protocol. Results do not constitute a security certification or establish real-world attack-detection rates. Read README_ZENODO.md and the archive's README.md before reproducing the results. Archive version: v3.1.

title: A Transferable Argument-Structure Direction in Eight Language Models: Causally Sufficient, Partially Necessary, and Robust to Linear Erasure
abstract: English verbs differ in how many arguments they require. We ask whether that structural property is encoded as a direction in a language model's residual stream, whether the direction is causally used, and whether it corresponds across model families. Across eight base models from six laboratories (1.4B-9.2B parameters), a single linear direction at the verb token predicts a model-supplied target - the log-odds of an argument-initial continuation over an adjunct-initial one - for verbs it was never fitted on (r = 0.418-0.606, all p = 0.005 against a permutation null). On intervention it raises argument continuation while suppressing adjunct continuation in all eight models. The direction transfers. Carried into another model's residual space through a ridge map fitted on generic prose with no argument-structure supervision, it moves the recipient's behaviour at a median 6.76x a random direction transported identically, recovering a median 99.9% of native effect across eight pairs. It is nonetheless a partial account. Removing it costs a median 13.9% of the behavioural distinction, where five rank-matched random directions move it by a median of -0.03% -- they raise it slightly as often as they lower it -- so every model's fitted removal is at least 91x its own control, yet 83.5-92.3% survives. Iterated removal exhausts linear decodability after a median of 7.5 directions while sixteen removals leave a median 60% of behaviour intact: the signal is used more than it is linearly decodable at that site. All experiments ran on a single Apple M1 Max with 32 GB unified memory.

title: Representative Photovoltaic Scenario Extraction Using Graph Clustering Models
abstract: This chapter addresses the challenge of extracting representative scenarios from multiple photovoltaic (PV) stations, where strong uncertainty and spatiotemporal correlations complicate power system optimization. A novel adaptive weighted two-layer graph clustering model is presented. At the local level, an adaptive nearest-neighbor graph with sparsity-promoting feature weights is learned for each station to emphasize critical daily periods and suppress irrelevant temporal variations. At the global level, these local graphs are fused into a consensus graph via learnable fusion weights, and a Laplacian rank constraint is imposed to automatically determine the optimal number of clusters without manual tuning. An alternating direction optimization algorithm is derived, with theoretically proven monotonic convergence guarantees. As a complementary pathway, this chapter presents an end-to-end deep adaptive graph neural network that jointly learns node embeddings and iteratively refines a learnable adjacency matrix through a clustering-oriented multi-objective loss function. The proposed methods are validated on three real-world datasets, namely the Australian PV dataset, ERA5 reanalysis data, and the Open Power System Data (OPSD), demonstrating superior cluster compactness, separation, and spatial correlation preservation over state-of-the-art benchmarks. Probabilistic power flow analysis on the IEEE 69-bus system further confirms the physical feasibility of the extracted scenarios under realistic network constraints.

title: Images Talk Back: Guiding MMDiTs by Suppressing Image-to-Text Feedback
abstract: Multimodal diffusion transformers (MMDiTs) allow the evolving image to update internal text representations through joint attention. These representations then guide subsequent image updates, raising a question: does this feedback help correct deviations from the prompt, or preserve them? We find that image-to-text (I2T) feedback can preserve the objects and attributes already represented in the evolving image, including errors. Transplanting I2T messages can rescue failures or disrupt successes. At matched intervention strengths, suppressing the influence of I2T feedback improves generation, whereas opposite controls degrade it. These findings motivate Semantic Feedback Guidance (SFG), which suppresses the influence of I2T feedback by guiding away from an auxiliary branch that strengthens this feedback and weakens text-to-image conditioning. The in-place variant, iSFG, directly suppresses I2T feedback and strengthens text-to-image conditioning, requiring no extra model evaluations. Temporal interventions motivate running the SFG branch during the first 20% of image sampling steps, requiring about $1.2\times$ the base NFE without classifier-free guidance (CFG). Experiments across three image-generation backbones show gains in alignment and preference-model scores. On FLUX, adding SFG to CFG raises GenEval from $0.6661$ to $0.7479$; on SD3.5M, iSFG adds $+1.33$ HPSv2.1 over CFG at zero extra NFE. The control also transfers to text-to-video and image-to-video generation, improving VBench scores. Code is available at https://github.com/yyc1215lll-creator/SFG.

title: Verifiable Retrieval for Legal Reasoning through Structure-driven Knowledge Graph
abstract: Any automation within reliability-critical contexts such as medicine or law has to be transparent and verifiable. Despite their advantages, current LLM-based systems do not meet these requirements due to their inherent black-box nature. Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) attempts to ground the generative process in the relevant interpretable documents, thereby reducing the risk of AI 'hallucinations' and potentially enabling verification of the initial generation context. However, as the number and size of potential sources increases, naive retrieval approaches tend to perform worse, ignoring critical context elements. In this paper we aim to tackle this problem in the context of German Legal Code. Using structure-driven parsing to create a Knowledge Graph (KG) for the source document navigation and retrieval, we compare several KG-informed chunking and retrieval strategies and evaluate their effect on the accuracy of retrieved citations.

title: On Privacy Mechanism Design Under a Bounded $α$-Lift Leakage Constraint with $χ^2$-Utility
abstract: We study the design of a statistical privacy mechanism under a bounded $α$-lift leakage constraint. An agent observes useful data $Y$, which is arbitrarily correlated with private data $X$, and releases $U$. The goal is to maximize Pearson $χ^2$-information $χ^2(Y;U)$ while satisfying the point-wise privacy constraint. This utility is an $f$-information that is nonnegative, obeys data processing, and measures the aggregate normalized change from the prior $P_Y$ to the posteriors $P_{Y|U=u}$. The main benefit of this choice is that $χ^2(Y;U)$ is exactly quadratic in the posterior perturbations; hence, no local approximation of the utility is required. For the nonlinear $α$-lift constraint, we derive a uniform Taylor-remainder bound that remains valid for the optimizing, $ε$-dependent perturbation. When $P_{X|Y}$ is invertible, this yields a closed-form quadratic surrogate, an explicitly scaled binary mechanism that satisfies the original $α$-lift constraint, a computable sufficient range for $ε$, and an $O(ε^{3/2})$ bound on the utility gap. For $α=2$, the solution is exact over an explicit range. We transfer these results to point-wise Rényi-divergence privacy, including an exact-feasible mechanism, an explicit privacy-budget range, and matching gap bounds. We also give an exact formulation for arbitrary leakage matrices and evaluate exact-feasible mechanisms numerically.

title: Neural network-based multipartite entanglement classification with prior guidance from quantum uncertainty relations
abstract: Quantum entanglement is a crucial resource in quantum information processing, yet its efficient, scalable and robust classification in multipartite systems remains theoretically challenging. Although supervised machine-learning has been applied to this task, most existing methods still suffer from high measurement costs, computational consumption, and weak noise robustness. In this work, by incorporating multipartite uncertainty relations as prior guidance, we propose a neural network approach to classify distinct Stochastic Local Operations and Classical Communication (SLOCC) multipartite entanglement classes based on states sampled from their local unitary (LU) orbits. Compared with traditional techniques, our method reduces experimental measurement-resource requirements and computational overhead, showing high adaptability to large-scale systems. The classification accuracy of our method reaches 99.5% in 20-qubit systems. The numerical validation is performed on states generated by random LU transformations, which preserve the SLOCC class. Within this setting, the proposed method offers strong effectiveness, scalability, and robustness for multipartite entanglement classification.

title: NewsSum-Bench: Comparative Benchmarking of Abstractive Text Summarization using Transformer Architectures (T5, BART, PEGASUS, mT5, BERT)
abstract: Initial release of the NewsSum-Bench research framework and benchmark for abstractive text summarization. Key Features & Contents:- Multi-model fine-tuning pipelines and evaluation notebooks for state-of-the-art Transformer architectures (T5, BART, PEGASUS, mT5, and BERT).- Custom data processing and preprocessing scripts for sentence tokenization.- Quantitative evaluation utilizing ROUGE metrics (ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2, ROUGE-L).- Interactive Streamlit web interface prototype for real-time article summarization.

title: RAG vs. GraphRAG for Industrial Technical Documentation: A Controlled Evaluation on Laser Manufacturing Manuals
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) enables large language models to answer questions grounded in external documents, yet its effectiveness on specialized industrial documentation remains underexplored. We present, to our knowledge, the first controlled comparison of conventional vector-based RAG and graph-augmented RAG (GraphRAG) on a laser-manufacturing operators manual. Both systems are evaluated on 1,000 queries sharing identical chunking (1,000-character segments, 200-character overlap), embedding (nomic-embed-text), generation (Gemma 3 12B via Ollama), and on-premises hardware (RTX 4090, 64 GB RAM). Retrieval accuracy is low for both architectures: baseline RAG achieves Hit@5 of 32.50% (MRR 0.217) and GraphRAG reaches 34.70% (MRR 0.229). However, GraphRAG improves faithfulness from 71.60% to 86.90% (+15.3 pp), suggesting that graph-augmented retrieval reduces hallucination even when chunk-level retrieval precision improves only marginally. Error analysis identifies four manufacturing-specific failure categories (navigational queries, technical identifiers, command syntax, and figure references) that are absent from general-domain RAG benchmarks. These results indicate that, in this industrial setting, retrieval quality rather than generation capability is the primary performance bottleneck, and point toward hybrid retrieval strategies for safety-critical manufacturing environments.

title: CCSD: a colloquial Chinese sentiment dataset with multi-dimensional linguistic perturbation for robustness benchmarking
abstract: Existing Chinese sentiment benchmarks are dominated by formally written text. Real user-generated content—including product reviews, social media posts, and online conversations—shares many colloquial phenomena with human-robot dialogue, such as dialect expressions, internet slang, emoji, incomplete utterances, and sarcasm. A classifier tuned on clean text has no reason to generalize to this distribution, yet there is no established benchmark for quantifying the gap. CCSD is therefore intended not only for sentiment benchmarking but also for robustness evaluation of conversational language understanding modules deployed in conversational robots. It contains 6,000 Chinese text samples, each perturbed through a subset of ten strategies that span four linguistic levels: lexical (dialect substitution, phonetic respelling), pragmatic (sarcastic suffixes, conflicting-context preambles), syntactic (rhetorical questions, inverted word order), and surface (internet slang, emoji, modal particles, truncation). Five traditional classifiers were evaluated on CCSD. Linear SVM achieved 83.17% accuracy at 0.16ms per sample on commodity CPU hardware. BERT-base achieved 98.54% accuracy with 92ms CPU latency and 13.57ms GPU latency. These efficiency findings directly inform model selection for service robots and edge-deployed conversational agents where GPU access is limited.

title: Toward scalable nonlinearities in convolutional optical neural networks driven by ultrashort laser pulses
abstract: The realization of ultrafast, low-power optical neural networks requires physically embedded nonlinear activation mechanisms compatible with Fourier-based photonic architectures. We demonstrate a convolutional optical neural network (OCNN) driven by a femtosecond-pulsed telecom laser, enabling intrinsic nonlinear activation via material absorption rather than electronic post-processing. Convolution is implemented in the Fourier plane using a spatial light modulator (SLM), with Laguerre-Gaussian modes serving as an orthogonal kernel basis. Object information is encoded directly onto the beam and processed through parallel Fourier-domain filtering. Nonlinear activation arises from two-photon absorption (TPA) in a CMOS camera, providing an intensity-dependent response without external electronic nonlinearities while remaining compatible with telecom wavelengths. The high peak intensities of ultrashort pulses enable scalable nonlinear activation at low average power. In object classification tasks, we achieve >90% accuracy, comparable to state-of-the-art OCNNs, establishing a pathway toward scalable, all-optical neuromorphic processors.

title: Reproducibility of social science research using aggregate statistics with noise infused for differential privacy
abstract: Privacy-preserving analytics such as differential privacy are designed to allow the analysis of sensitive datasets while protecting individuals' privacy. Their deployment, however, has been controversial. Critics maintain that statistical noise injected to preserve privacy can degrade the quality and feasibility of social science research. We select a benchmark of empirical findings from 93 published social science studies involving regression analyses over aggregate statistics. We evaluate whether their findings replicate on privacy noise-infused data. Under privacy budgets typical in industry, around 91% of simulated findings still support the original claims at significance level [Formula: see text]. Claims based on weaker original effect sizes are more likely to be nullified or sometimes reversed. We compare distortions caused by privacy noise to those due to measurement errors and other kinds of nonsampling errors common in social statistics, and we find that the marginal impacts of privacy protection are smaller. Moreover, discrepancies due to privacy noise are often much smaller than discrepancies observed in traditional replication and robustness studies.

title: Physical Side-Channel Attacks on Edge LLMs: Extracting Output Tokens and User Prompts
abstract: The deployment of large language models (LLMs) on edge devices is largely motivated by privacy concerns over sharing sensitive user data with cloud servers. In this paper, we demonstrate that keeping inference local does not eliminate privacy risks: an adversary with physical access to the device may exploit hardware leakage to recover sensitive information without compromising or modifying the software system. In particular, we present an electromagnetic (EM) side-channel attack targeting LLM inference on edge devices. Targeting LLaMA-3.2-1B-Instruct running on a Raspberry Pi 5, we demonstrate that EM traces collected during inference can leak both generated tokens and user prompts. We propose three attacks under different threat assumptions. First, a profiling attack that identifies generated tokens among 50 medical and privacy-related keywords with 97.2% accuracy on profiled words. Second, a reconstruction attack recovers the model's hidden representations and uses them to predict tokens from the full 128k-token vocabulary, achieving 94.3% accuracy on profiled classes. For unseen words, the correct token is ranked within the first 100 positions of the 128k-token vocabulary in 67% of cases, with a median rank of 54. Finally, we present a hidden-state inversion attack that uses the recovered hidden state to reconstruct user prompts semantically. Our proposed attacks require only passive EM side-channel measurements and a limited number of traces during model training. These results demonstrate that local execution alone may not guarantee the confidentiality of generated tokens and user inputs.

title: How Much Computation Does Every Forecast Need? Structured Block Skipping in Two Time-Series Foundation Models
abstract: Time-series foundation models use the same network depth for every input, although forecasting windows differ in structure and difficulty. We test whether whole Transformer blocks can be removed at inference time in two pretrained models: Chronos-Bolt and TimesFM 2.5. Our bypasses avoid the original block computation and preserve the dense model exactly when all blocks are enabled. Masks are selected only on calibration windows and evaluated on 1,088 held-out windows from ETTh1, Traffic, Weather, and Exchange. At moderate sparsity, Chronos-Bolt with 7/11 candidate blocks and TimesFM with 16/20 blocks show little change in mean relative forecasting quality across datasets while reducing median A100 batch-1 latency by 11.2% and 13.4%. More aggressive TimesFM skipping accelerates inference further but substantially harms Traffic and Weather. Across both models, different equal-budget masks win on different windows, and a retrospective oracle significantly improves over the best static mask on every dataset. However, dataset-specific masks transfer inconsistently, and Chronos representations do not support reliable unseen-domain routing. These results establish cross-architecture structured redundancy and input-dependent opportunity, but not a deployable dynamic inference method.

title: Pulsed control of an entanglement-breaking index: thermal valleys, a certified valve, and its open-close asymmetry
abstract: The entanglement-breaking index of a channel is the number of self-compositions after which all entanglement with a reference system is destroyed. In a thermal qubit collision loop whose round is affine in the bath polarisation p, some circuits have thermal valleys: on an interior window of p the index falls below its infinite-temperature value. Rounds at different p compose exactly, so every schedule of polarisations defines a composite channel whose entanglement-breaking status can be certified in ball arithmetic. A gated search of 33 million random circuits finds no valley with contrast above about 3e-3, with an interior maximum near index 90, and yields six certified targets. At the reference target, held inside its window for 88 rounds, a centred excursion to p = 0.05 restores entanglement at exactly eight rounds: every shorter centred pulse certifiably fails, and so do the same eight rounds at the start. A 53-round pulse certifiably beats the static protocol, a depth-three valley is walked down its staircase by pulse duration, and a 1.2 per cent coherent tilt of the ancilla opens the switch at fixed population. Closing the switch costs 21 to 35 rounds. The asymmetry is not one of local rates, which agree to within about two per cent at matched circuit positions (certified). It is one of distance and response: closing must remove an entanglement margin 2.2 times larger, and while hot rounds added to a window hold act almost independently, window rounds added to a hot hold act collectively. Near the crossing, the lever of the log-margin is that of a linear approach to the entanglement-breaking boundary, with no free parameter. At the reference target, depolarising noise of about $4ν/n$ per round kills a signature of size $ν$ read after $n$ rounds: 1.3e-4 for the static signal, 6.5e-6 for the eight-round switch.

title: Perspectives on Effective Use of Large Language Models in Statistical Consulting and Collaboration Settings
abstract: As large language models (LLMs) become increasingly capable of mimicking statistical reasoning, performing data cleaning and standard analyses and assisting in data interpretation, statistical consulting faces a transformative opportunity. In this session, experienced statistical consultants discussed the ways in which AI has impacted their work. This included the utilization of private LLMs to enhance efficiency of services, the changes in how we train our consultants and interact with clients, and the innovations in statistical communication. In addition, important ethical considerations were discussed. Each panelist gave a 10 to 15-minute overview highlighting one of these impacts and the remainder of the session was devoted to a panel discussion with the audience. This paper collects and extends material presented at an invited panel at the 2026 Joint Statistical Meetings in Boston.

title: A commutative group action-based framework for asymmetric anamorphic encryption
abstract: Anamorphic encryption is a cryptographic paradigm that allows covert messages to be hidden inside ordinary ciphertexts of a public-key encryption scheme. The covert channel is enabled by a secret double-key shared between the sender and an authorized receiver. Even if an adversary coerces the receiver into revealing the secret-key, the hidden communication remains undetectable without the double-key. Existing formulations of asymmetric anamorphic encryption suffer from two limitations. First, key pairs of a public-key encryption scheme and double-keys are tightly coupled: once a public-key is deployed, it is no longer possible to associate fresh double-keys with it. Second, existing constructions of asymmetric anamorphic encryption either rely on additional cryptographic primitives or on stronger structural assumptions, or they are scheme-specific.In this work, we refine the syntax of asymmetric anamorphic encryption so that double-key generation is separated from key deployment, allowing multiple double-keys to be registered with the same public-key after setup. We then construct an asymmetric anamorphic encryption scheme from the group-action-based public-key encryption scheme $ \mathsf{gaPKE} $, which is built from a regular effective group action over a commutative group. The resulting scheme is secure in the standard model. Our construction combines a hybrid encryption scheme, built under the $ \textsf{GA-DDH}$ assumption and entropy smoothing of hash functions, with a second independent group-action instance that carries the covert message. The resulting scheme satisfies anamorphic security, sender indistinguishability under chosen-plaintext attack security and colluder indistinguishability under chosen-plaintext attack security. We instantiate our framework in both post-quantum and classical settings. Using $ \textsf{CSIDH}$ group actions, we obtain the first isogeny-based asymmetric anamorphic encryption scheme. Using $ \textsf{DDH}$-hard groups, we obtain a classical anamorphic encryption scheme based on hashed ElGamal.

title: Federated Flight Anomaly Detection with Self-Supervised Forecasting: A Flight-Disjoint Evaluation
abstract: Reliable anomaly detection is essential for the safe operation of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), particularly in distributed settings where flight telemetry is generated across multiple vehicles or operational sessions and cannot always be centrally collected. This work investigates UAV anomaly detection using models capable of generalizing to unseen flights while keeping raw telemetry within the simulated client partitions during federated training. A self-supervised forecasting framework is evaluated under a simulated federated partitioning of the ALFA corpus and benchmarked using local training, Federated Averaging (FedAvg), FedProx, personalized FedAvg, and centralized learning under a strictly flight-disjoint evaluation protocol. The evaluation comprises 47 complete flights, including 36 failed and 11 nominal flights, grouped into 13 heterogeneous session-based federated clients that serve as statistical partitions rather than physically independent UAVs. The resulting federated setting exhibits non-IID characteristics due to differences in local flight composition and data volume across clients. Federated training is performed for 20 communication rounds with two local epochs per round, and evaluation uses three-fold flight-disjoint cross-validation. Complete flights, including failed flights, are assigned exclusively to either the training or held-out test partition within each fold, ensuring that no samples or overlapping windows from a test flight contribute to model training. An LSTM learns nominal flight dynamics through multivariate next-step forecasting, and the resulting forecasting error is converted into an anomaly score. FedAvg achieves an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.908 and detects 83.3% of failed flights, performing competitively with centralized learning, which obtains an AUC of 0.904 and an 84.4% detection rate. Beyond discrimination performance, calibration, threshold scope, temporal persistence, detection delay, and false-alarm burden are also evaluated. With rolling calibration and a global threshold, the detector maintains an 87.2% flight-level detection rate with a median detection delay of 0.72 s while reducing the false-alarm burden from 202.1 to 66.0 events per hour. However, this alarm frequency remains too high for unattended operational deployment. A more conservative configuration reduces the burden to 8.17 events per hour while retaining 82.8% failed-flight detection and achieving an event precision of 0.851, although the median detection delay increases to 3.38 s. Within this session-partitioned experimental setting, parameter aggregation recovers most of the performance loss associated with local-only training and approaches centralized performance without pooling raw telemetry. These findings should be interpreted as evidence for distributed model aggregation under statistical data partitioning rather than as validation of a fully deployed federated UAV network, while the operational analysis further shows that strong discrimination and flight-level detection do not necessarily translate into practically acceptable alarm behavior.

title: An urban patrol case urgency classification method based on self-supervised clustering of a graph neural network
abstract: Accurate assessment of urban patrol cases plays an important role in maintaining urban safety and improving the efficiency of urban governance. The hazard level of urban patrol cases can be reflected by the urgency level and prioritizing high-urgency cases can help reduce potential risks to public safety. However, it remains challenging to assess the urgency level of urban patrol cases when reliable urgency labels are limited or unavailable. To address this problem, this paper proposes an urban patrol case urgency classification method based on self-supervised clustering of a graph neural network. First, a case-relationship graph is constructed from urban patrol cases. A graph attention-based autoencoder is then pretrained to learn node representations, and K-means is used to initialize cluster centers. Finally, representation learning and clustering are jointly optimized to identify urgency-oriented clusters without using manual labels during training. Experimental validation was conducted using 6126 urban patrol case records from Zhengzhou, China. The proposed method achieved a Recall of 0.7458, Precision of 0.7465, ACC of 0.7424, F1 of 0.7403, and NMI of 0.4517. Compared with TADW, the strongest baseline, the proposed method improved these metrics by 0.0617, 0.0479, 0.0650, 0.0690, and 0.0407, respectively. These results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively learn urgency-related latent representations and improve the classification quality of urban patrol cases.

title: Constructive Bounds for the Topological Expressivity of Neural Networks
abstract: The expressivity of a neural network $Φ$ describes the class of functions that a network can express. The term topological expressivity refers to a family of measures particularly suited to understand binary classification and is often formulated in terms of the Betti numbers of a decision boundary $β(Φ^{-1}(0))$. Despite its popularity, this measure is not as useful for regression and other problems that do not involve a decision boundary. Instead, we propose to study topological expressivity in terms of the Betti numbers of the output of a neural network $β(Φ(X))$. We formally prove that a ReLU network with architecture $(d,\sum\limits_{k=1}^{d } β_k(3k+2),\sum\limits_{k=1}^{d}β_k(k+1))$ can express spaces homotopy equivalent to wedge sums of spheres with arbitrary Betti numbers. This gives upper bounds for any arbitrary connected ($β_0=1$) sequence of Betti numbers, but by constructing spaces homotopy equivalent to products of $N$ spheres of dimension $d_1,...,d_N$ we achieve much better bounds $(\sum\limits_{n=1} d_n, 3\sum\limits_{n=1}\limits^N d_n + 2N, \sum\limits_{n=1}\limits^N d_n + N) $ for Betti numbers given by $\prod_n (1+x^{d_n})$. Finally we conjecture a much stronger tight bound which gives the architectural bound $(d,d+1,d+1)$ for a space homeomorphic to the sphere.

title: Collective Autonomous Vehicle Routing Needs Social Awareness for Coexistence with Human Drivers
abstract: Collective Autonomous Vehicle (AV) route choices in real-world traffic networks can create externalities for Human-Driven Vehicles (HDVs), as routes that benefit AVs may increase travel times for other road users. To address this, we introduce a social component, the marginal cost, to the selfish travel time AV reward. Marginal cost captures an AV's impact on other road users by comparing their travel times with those in a counterfactual simulation in which the AV is removed. We study AV route choice in mixed-autonomy traffic settings using Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL), where AVs learn routing policies through repeated interactions with the traffic environment. Experiments on the real-world networks of Ingolstadt and Provins show that incorporating marginal cost into the AV reward not only limits the increase in HDV travel times and shortens AV travel times relative to selfish AV routing, but also improves overall system performance. In Ingolstadt, selfish routing of 40\% AVs increases the travel times of other vehicles by 1.7\%, and this drops to 1.1\% when the social reward is included. Interestingly, not only does overall system performance improve, but the AVs are also better off when acting socially.This effect is consistent across tested cities, penetration rates, and replications, yet when the weight of the social component in the reward increases, the system fails to reach the desired performance. For a more scalable approach to social AV routing in mixed-autonomy traffic, we compute the marginal cost only for the AVs whose route choices most affect the traffic system. This reduces the number of counterfactual simulations and achieves similar performance at a significantly lower computational cost. Our results suggest that AV routing should go beyond selfish rewards and, for the benefit of all traffic participants, include a social component in its objective.

title: SharP: Soft and Hard Prompt-Guided Augmentation with LLM for Low Resource Fake News Detection
abstract: Fake news detection under low resource conditions is challenged by the scarcity of labeled data and the difficulty of capturing subtle deceptive patterns. In this work, we focus on low resource fake news detection, where only a small labeled set is available for training, while evaluation is performed under a fixed and unchanged test protocol. This setting is motivated by costly, ambiguous fact-checking and emerging topics and domains that are poorly covered by existing benchmarks. Existing data augmentation methods, such as synonym substitution, generative adversarial networks, and large language model (LLM)-based generation, often produce fluent but overly generic content, lacking the task-specific relevance needed for accurate detection. To address this, we propose SharP, a boundary-aware text generation framework guided by soft and hard prompts, which leverages LLMs as tools adapted to produce task-specific synthetic samples. SharP employs a dual prompt mechanism: hard prompts provide structured guidance and factual constraints, while soft prompts introduce learned semantic patterns from the data. These two types of prompts are combined to guide the generation process, enabling the model to produce samples that closely align with the characteristics of news. To further enhance detection performance, we incorporate a boundary-aware strategy that steers generation toward areas where the classifier is less confident, helping to clarify subtle distinctions between real and fake content. In addition, we adopt a dual objective optimization that balances semantic alignment with the source data and classifier feedback. This encourages the generation of samples that are both domain-consistent and helpful for refining decision boundaries, ultimately improving model robustness and generalization in low resource fake news detection.

title: Minions: A Dynamic and Distributed Virtual GPU Cloud Built on Idle Apple Silicon Devices
abstract: The increasing demand for GPU-accelerated machine learning inference has exposed limitations in centralized GPU infrastructures, including high cost, limited elasticity, and long wait times under resource constraints. At the same time, modern Apple Silicon-based macOS devices are equipped with powerful GPUs that remain largely idle during normal usage. This paper presents Minions, a dynamic and distributed virtual GPU cloud that aggregates idle Apple Silicon GPUs across macOS devices to execute large-scale machine learning inference workloads. Minions enables teams to leverage existing hardware without requiring additional GPU procurement. The system provides flexible GPU inference task execution, fault tolerance, and efficient resource utilization. Our experience shows that idle macOS devices can be transformed into a practical distributed GPU inference platform in environments where centralized GPU resources are constrained.

title: Quantum-assisted rendezvous on hypercubes: a quantum Bernoulli noise approach
abstract: We study quantum-assisted balanced rendezvous on the $d$-dimensional hypercube in a one-step two-agent quantum-walk framework, where the two agents move the same Hamming distance and meet at a common midpoint. The key structure is a projective $t$-sphere resolution, which governs exact finite-dimensional quantum attainment. Its scalar analogue recovers the corresponding classical characterization. We characterize finite-dimensional quantum attainment of the no-signalling benchmark, construct quantum strategies from projective sphere resolutions, and establish a rigidity theorem for optimal finite-dimensional strategies. A marked difference appears between nearest-neighbor and higher-cardinality updates: quantum advantage can occur in the former, whereas in the latter the geometry of the relevant Hamming spheres rules out exact finite-dimensional attainment of the no-signalling value. Together, these results connect quantum-walk dynamics, Hamming-sphere geometry, and quantum rendezvous within the quantum Bernoulli noises (QBN) framework.

Shuningdek, o'quvchilarning mantiqiy fikrlashi, muammolarni hal etish (problem-solving) qobiliyatlari va muhandislik tafakkurini rivojlantirishda ta'limiy robototexnikaning didaktik imkoniyatlari tahlil qilingan hamda amaliy tavsiyalar berilgan.

title: pssgp: physical-state-supervised Gaussian process surrogates
abstract: Python implementation of cross-fitted physical-state supervision for design-only scalar prediction, using a global Gaussian process and an optional soft mixture of GP experts. Version 0.1.0 includes a generic array/DataFrame interface, fold-local preprocessing, input-schema checks, a standalone thermal ODE example, tests, and archived experiment utilities. The software is licensed under the MIT License. Supporting research data are available separately at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23253596 under CC BY 4.0. Research datasets, ICF solver source and binaries, material tables, trajectories, model checkpoints and private run logs are excluded from this software release. The generic core and thermal example are independent of the ICF simulator; the archived ICF experiment utilities require the documented external frozen experiment archive. See README.md for installation, usage, validation and reproduction limitations.

title: Topological Inference Engine: Paraconsistent Thermodynamics in Silicon for Sub-Second Quantum Emulation
abstract: The current paradigm of high-performance computing (HPC) and quantum simulation is constrained by the Von Neumann bottleneck and the exponential memory explosion (O(2^N)) of Hilbert spaces. We introduce a fundamental paradigm shift: Paraconsistent Computing in Silicon. By replacing conditional branching with thermodynamic absorption in SRAM using Belnap's four-valued logic (L4), we demonstrate a Single-GPU architecture capable of resolving the 53-qubit Sycamore circuit in 783 milliseconds—a 380x time-to-solution improvement over the 41-million-core Sunway Supercomputer. This foundational technology unlocks microsecond-latency Quantum Error Correction (QEC) and 1RSB-hardened Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC). This document serves as the foundational whitepaper and technical due diligence for the Topological Inference Engine.

title: Zero-Divergence GF(2) Tensor Engines for Microsecond-Latency Quantum Error Correction Decoding
abstract: The realization of Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing (FTQC) is currently bottlenecked not by quantum hardware, but by classical decoding latency. Surface codes require classical coprocessors to identify and correct physical qubit errors well within the decoherence time window (T₁ ≈ 15 µs). Traditional graph-based decoders suffer from severe SIMT warp divergence when executed on highly parallel architectures, leading to ALU starvation and fatal latency spikes. In this paper, we introduce a branchless GF(2) tensor engine that entirely suppresses warp divergence (0.0%). Operating directly within the L2 Cache of a consumer-grade GPU (60W TDP), our architecture processes 1,000,000 Clifford gates across 2,560 logical qubits in 5.36 seconds, achieving a sustained throughput of 0.95 G-TOPS. This translates to a decoding latency of 5.36 µs per parallel gate, successfully operating within the strict decoherence threshold and providing a scalable classical infrastructure for real-time Quantum Error Correction. For strict artifact evaluation, the source code and reproducibility harnesses are publicly available at https://github.com/MAJBS/Chronos-Dialeteia-Engine.

title: RememberMe - Dataset
abstract: This dataset contains the experimental data used to evaluate the RememberMe multimodal memory-assistance system. The dataset includes face images and live-webcam frames used for visitor recognition, together with audio recordings used to evaluate speech-to-text performance under different speech conditions. The data supports the experimental evaluation of face recognition, speech recognition, conversation processing, and end-to-end system performance reported in the associated research paper.

title: Electronic–photonic neuromorphic spiking based on an RTD-Driven InP laser
abstract: An electronic-photonic spiking node consisting of a resonant tunneling diode (RTD) driving a waveguide-integrated O-band DFB laser, both fabricated in separate indium phosphide (InP) chips, is demonstrated. We investigate the excitability of the RTD-laser spiking node and demonstrate input-dependent bursting with a 12-33 kHz burst frequency and a 9 MHz spiking frequency in each burst. We show this bursting is caused by the RTD alternately driving the laser below and above threshold. We also investigate the use of the RTD-laser as a source of modulated light by DC biasing the RTD in its negative differential region. These results highlight the potential of RTD–laser neuromorphic nodes as building blocks for hybrid electronic–photonic spiking neural networks, enabling efficient information processing across electrical and optical domains with scalable bandwidth, low-energy operation and native compatibility with event-driven, threshold-based processing.

title: Transformer-based In-Context Score Operator Learning for Diffusion Models
abstract: Diffusion models typically learn the generative dynamics of a single target distribution or a family of distributions indexed by conditioning variables fixed during training. This limits their ability to adapt to a previously unseen distribution from only a small set of examples. We introduce an in-context solution operator learning framework for diffusion models, in which each target distribution is treated as a task drawn from a meta-distribution and is specified at inference time by an empirical context set. Our method learns an in-context score operator that maps the context samples, a noisy query point, and the diffusion time to the task-dependent score, enabling reverse-diffusion sampling on unseen tasks without retraining or parameter updates. A key observation is that the task-dependent score admits a Gaussian-kernel conditional-mean representation. Its empirical Nadaraya--Watson approximation can be represented exactly by a model in our constructed transformer class, providing a principled foundation for the proposed query-dependent attention architecture. The operator is trained through amortized denoising score matching across task distributions. We establish generalization-error bounds that quantify the effects of the context size, the numbers of training tasks and within-task samples, model complexity, and intrinsic and ambient dimensions. Numerically, we evaluate the method on a range of scientific and visual datasets, including Navier-Stokes, ERA5 climate data, QuickDraw sketches, and Food-101. The results show that the proposed method performs well on relatively simple task families, while its performance degrades as task complexity increases, thereby illustrating both the promise and the limitations of in-context learning for diffusion models.

title: Retrieval Quality, Evidence, and Appropriate Abstention in Large Language Models
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) can give fluent and useful answers, but they can also produce information that is false or not supported by evidence. This problem is often called hallucination. In this paper, we study how the quality of the evidence retrieved is associated with differences in the answers given by an LLM. The experiment used 13 questions in English, Hindi, and Gujarati. The questions were tested under three conditions: No Retrieval, High-quality Retrieval, and Low-quality Retrieval. In total, the experiment produced 117 responses. The responses were evaluated using factual correctness, evidence support, appropriate abstention, over-cautious behavior, unsupported inference, and non-evaluable cases. In the No Retrieval condition, all 39 responses were fully correct. In the High-quality Retrieval condition, 34 of 36 evaluable responses were fully correct. In the Low-quality Retrieval condition, only 3 of 39 responses were fully correct, but 36 responses showed appropriate abstention. This means that the model often responded that the evidence was not sufficient instead of making an unsupported claim. The results suggest that retrieval does not automatically improve the reliability of an LLM. The quality, relevance and completeness of the evidence are also important. The study also shows that factual correctness, evidence faithfulness, and appropriate uncertainty should be evaluated separately.

title: Sobolev-Regularized Filtering on Weighted Riemannian State Spaces for Kinematic Signal Recovery at Very Low Signal-to-Noise Ratio
abstract: Recovering a kinematically coherent signal from observations whose signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) lies far below 0 dB is a central difficulty in radar tracking under electronic countermeasures. Classical linear filters treat the observation as an unstructured scalar sequence and, at very low SNR, either discard the signal or require model assumptions that an adversary can violate. This paper develops a variational framework in which the observation is represented as a scalar field on a five-dimensional weighted Riemannian state space (planar position, planar velocity, acceleration magnitude) and is estimated by minimizing a variable-exponent Sobolev energy that couples a second-order smoothness penalty with a spatially adaptive data-fidelity term. We (i) establish existence and uniqueness of the minimizer, (ii) derive the optimality condition, including a curvature correction missing from the flat-space form, (iii) give a spectral bias-variance analysis showing that the estimator behaves as an adaptive low-pass filter whose achievable noise reduction is governed by the ratio of the observation dimension to the effective signal dimension, and (iv) obtain a mean-square error rate that matches the classical minimax exponent for Sobolev classes. Interactive Benchmark & Live Demo: https://5dvr.ai
